title: The Fermionic Cohomology Problem On The Full Fock Space Is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-Complete
authors: Yibin Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermionic cohomology characterizes the zero-energy states of the supersymmetric Hamiltonian associated with a fermionic differential. Previous work showed that the problem restricted to a particle-number sector specified with the input is [MATH]-hard and belongs to [MATH]. We study the global problem, in which no sector is specified and cohomology may occur anywhere in the full Fock space. This formulation directly matches the whole-space ground-state question: a specified-degree NO instance may still have zero-energy states in another sector, whereas the global NO promise excludes them across all sectors and their superpositions. We prove that this full-Fock problem is [MATH]-complete for differentials given as exact lists of local monomials, even when each monomial acts on at most [MATH] modes. As a companion result, we prove [MATH]-completeness for the specified-degree problem with [MATH]-mode terms whose hard instances admit a one-dimensional block-chain realization.
tldr: The paper proves that the fermionic cohomology problem on the full Fock space is QMA_1-complete.
motivation: This problem characterizes zero-energy states of supersymmetric Hamiltonians; previous work only considered fixed particle-number sectors, but the global problem matches whole-space ground-state questions.
method: The authors prove completeness by showing that instances with differentials given as exact lists of local monomials (each acting on at most k modes) encode QMA_1 problems.
result: They prove that the full-Fock cohomology problem is QMA_1-complete, and also establish QMA_1-completeness for a specified-degree problem with 2-mode terms under a block-chain realization.
conclusion: This addresses the complexity of the global fermionic cohomology problem, contrasting with earlier sector-specific results.

title: Isospectral Potentials With Dirac Delta Interaction: Constrained Spectra
authors: Kumar Abhinav, Biswanath Rath, Prasanta K. Panigrahi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantum potentials containing Dirac delta function (DDF) within its supersymmetric (isospectral) construction via a discontinuous superpotential, instead of being simply an added part. This construction comprises of two independently solvable sectors joined at the singular point by matching conditions imposed by the corresponding self-adjoint extension. Needing careful regularization, these boundary conditions impose independent algebraic constraints on each of the eigenstates, that restrict and truncate the spectrum. The number of surviving bound states, which are required to be parity-even, is thus fixed by the available system parameters rather than by the usual quantization rule. The specific cases of the Harmonic oscillator and the Rosen-Morse potential isospectrally infused with the DDF demonstrate such highly restrictive spectra, while the similar combination of the DDF with a Calogero-type singularity turns out to be largely incompatible as the regularization breaks down. Therefore, localized singularities are capable of controlling and engineering the discrete spectrum of quantum systems, with possible use in myriads of physical systems with very localized interactions.
tldr: This paper investigates how a Dirac delta interaction within supersymmetric isospectral constructions constrains and truncates the bound state spectrum, with parity-even states surviving.
motivation: To understand how localized singular interactions can shape discrete spectra in solvable quantum potentials, potentially enabling spectral engineering.
method: Uses supersymmetric quantum mechanics with a discontinuous superpotential and self-adjoint extension matching conditions at the singular point to analyze two solvable sectors.
result: The matching conditions impose algebraic constraints that restrict and truncate the spectrum, fixing the number of bound states based on system parameters, demonstrated for harmonic oscillator and Rosen-Morse potentials, while Calogero-type singularities are incompatible.
conclusion: Localized delta-function interactions can effectively control and engineer discrete spectra, with potential applications in systems with highly localized interactions.

title: Generation Of Multicomponent Schr\"odinger Cat States In Schemes With Measurement Of Gaussian States
authors: S. B. Korolev E. A. Nesterova
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a scheme for generating superpositions of Fock states whose numbers differ by four or eight. The proposed protocol is based on photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states. We compare of the generated states with multicomponent Schr\"odinger cat states. We evaluate the fidelity and determine how it scales with the number of detected particles. Furthermore, we derive the optimal configuration for the generation such states.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate superpositions of Fock states using photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states, aiming to produce multicomponent Schrödinger cat states.
motivation: The generation of specific non-classical quantum states is important for quantum information processing, and this protocol offers a way to create multicomponent cat states.
method: The scheme uses photon-number-resolving measurements on multimode Gaussian states to generate superpositions of Fock states with photon numbers differing by four or eight. Fidelity is evaluated and scaling with detected particles is analyzed.
result: The fidelity of the generated states compared to ideal Schrödinger cat states is assessed, and the optimal configuration for generation is derived.
conclusion: The work provides a scheme for generating multicomponent Schrödinger cat states with high fidelity, contributing to quantum state engineering.

title: Spatial Correlations Of Photons Interacting Via Transverse Rydberg Blockade
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Daniil Svirskiy, Matthias Metternich, Wolfgang Alt, Sebastian Hofferberth, Ofer Firstenberg
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of the transverse spatial dynamics of two interacting photons in a Rydberg nonlinear medium. Extending the well-studied one-dimensional case, we explore both longitudinal and transverse correlations of photons propagating as Rydberg polaritons. We identify distinct behaviors and scaling laws for these correlations, arising from fundamentally different mechanisms in the two directions: diffraction for transverse correlations and diffusion for longitudinal correlations. We develop a model incorporating a Gaussian optical beam and an inhomogeneous atomic density distribution, from which we derive quantitative predictions for correlation functions in both directions. We further show that the propagation equations can be reduced to a single Schr\"odinger-like equation, allowing approximate solutions that are supported by full numerical results. Our findings indicate that the transverse correlation length is determined primarily by the blockade radius, whereas the longitudinal correlation length is limited by bandwidth. These results establish transverse Rydberg blockade as a distinct and measurable correlation mechanism and show that spatial photon correlations provide a direct means of measuring the blockade radius.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of transverse spatial correlations of two interacting photons in a Rydberg nonlinear medium, showing that the transverse correlation length is set by the blockade radius and longitudinal by bandwidth, and that these correlations can directly measure the blockade radius.
motivation: To extend the well-studied one-dimensional case of photon-photon interactions in Rydberg media to include transverse spatial dynamics, and to identify distinct mechanisms for correlations in different directions.
method: The authors model photon propagation as Rydberg polaritons in a medium with a Gaussian beam profile and inhomogeneous atomic density, derive correlation functions in both longitudinal and transverse directions, and reduce the propagation equations to a single Schrödinger-like equation, verified by numerical simulations.
result: They find that transverse correlations arise from diffraction and are governed by the blockade radius, while longitudinal correlations arise from diffusion and are limited by bandwidth, with distinct scaling laws.
conclusion: Transverse Rydberg blockade constitutes a distinct, measurable correlation mechanism, and spatial photon correlations offer a direct way to measure the blockade radius.

title: Parafermions In Plain Sight
authors: A. Chaudhary Siu A. Chin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for any potential with a discrete energy spectrum, the well-known interpolation between ideal boson and fermion partition functions at discrete values of [MATH] yielded zero temperature ground state energies corresponding to [MATH] fermions occupying a single quantum state. The grand canonical partition function in this case can be a result from genuine parastatistics.
tldr: This paper shows that the interpolation between boson and fermion partition functions at discrete values yields ground state energies corresponding to fermions in a single state, and that the grand canonical partition function can arise from genuine parastatistics.
motivation: To explore the theoretical connection between standard quantum statistics (bosons/fermions) and generalized parastatistics, potentially illuminating foundational aspects of quantum statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical derivation using the interpolation between bosonic and fermionic partition functions, evaluating ground state energies at discrete interpolation points, and demonstrating consistency with parastatistics.
result: The interpolation at specific values reproduces ground state energies of fermions occupying a single quantum state, and the grand canonical partition function can be interpreted as arising from genuine parastatistics.
conclusion: The findings suggest a deeper relationship between boson-fermion interpolation and parastatistics, which may have implications for understanding exotic quantum statistics.

title: Two-photon Quantum Rabi Models - Spectral Degeneracy And Symmetries
authors: Masato Wakayama Cid Reyes-Bustos
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum Rabi model occupies a distinguished role in the study of quantum light and matter, describing the most fundamental interactions. Elucidation of its spectral properties, along with those of its generalizations, is necessary for quantum optics and applications in areas such as quantum information technologies. In this paper, we explore a precise description of energy degeneracy of the two-photon asymmetric quantum Rabi model and the nature of the system's symmetries; as a result, we demonstrate that these have significant relationships with the structure of certain algebraic curves (hyperelliptic curves) and number theory. Concretely, we first prove the existence of degenerate eigenvalues using the monodromy data of the Fuchsian ODE, which draws the eigenvalue problem of the system, and the existence of associated symmetry operators, previously discovered and studied heuristically in physics. Subsequently, we give a complete characterization of spectral degeneracies and present a series of conjectures showing that the degeneracy may determine the entire energy spectral structure. More precisely, for sufficiently strong interaction, we obtain an excellent approximation of the energy curves by the zero locus of a two-variable polynomial associated to degenerate eigenstates. In addition, we postulate an explicit description of the relation between the missing symmetry at the Hamiltonian level (hidden symmetry) and the degeneracy of the two-photon quantum Rabi model.
tldr: The paper investigates spectral degeneracy and symmetries of the two-photon quantum Rabi model, connecting them to algebraic curves and number theory.
motivation: Understanding quantum Rabi model spectra is important for quantum optics and quantum information, but the paper is purely mathematical without direct ties to the stated research directions.
method: The authors use monodromy data of a Fuchsian ODE and prove results on degenerate eigenvalues and symmetry operators, also deriving polynomial approximations for energy curves.
result: They prove existence of degenerate eigenvalues, provide a complete characterization of degeneracies, and propose conjectures linking degeneracy to full spectral structure.
conclusion: The study reveals deep connections between spectral degeneracy and symmetries in the two-photon Rabi model, but is not directly relevant to the specified research interests.

title: Stochastic Optimization Of Tree Tensor Networks
authors: Marius Willner, Maximilian Scharf, Andr\'e Uschmajew, Timo Felser, Marco Trenti
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor networks, originally developed for quantum many-body physics, are promising models for machine learning. We derive stochastic Riemannian optimizers for tree tensor networks (TTNs) on both their parameter and quotient manifolds, including adaptive and learning-rate-free schemes suitable for minibatch training. Using a hybrid CNN-TTN architecture, we evaluate the methods on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, and Imagenette. The proposed optimizers achieve predictive performance comparable to unconstrained optimization while enabling numerically stable downstream compression.
tldr: This paper introduces stochastic Riemannian optimizers for tree tensor networks and demonstrates their effectiveness in hybrid CNN-TTN models for image classification tasks.
motivation: Tensor networks are promising models for machine learning, but optimization methods need to be adapted for their manifold structure.
method: Derives stochastic Riemannian optimizers on parameter and quotient manifolds of tree tensor networks, including adaptive and learning-rate-free schemes, and tests them with a hybrid CNN-TTN architecture.
result: The optimizers achieve predictive performance comparable to unconstrained optimization while enabling numerically stable downstream compression.
conclusion: The proposed optimizers are effective for training tensor network models in machine learning, offering stability and compression benefits.

title: Chern--Simons Fluctuations And Information Geometry In Discrete Electromagnetism
authors: Jean-Pierre Magnot
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct helicity-conditioned statistical states for a Whitney-discretized electromagnetic field on a closed oriented three-manifold. The simplicial de Rham complex provides exact discrete gauge symmetry, while the Whitney inner product separates exact, harmonic, and coexact sectors. The spatial Abelian Chern--Simons functional is gauge invariant and depends only on the coexact potential. After fixing harmonic modes, we introduce a helicity-biased Gaussian ensemble on the reduced electromagnetic phase space and derive explicit formulas for its admissible parameters, partition function, mean helicity, relative entropy, and Fisher information. The distribution uniquely minimizes relative entropy under a prescribed mean-helicity constraint. Its helicity susceptibility equals the variance of the discrete Chern--Simons functional and controls the local distinguishability of neighboring statistical states. Because magnetic helicity is generally not conserved under unconstrained Maxwell dynamics, these states represent conditioned inference rather than dynamical equilibrium.
tldr: This paper constructs helicity-constrained Gaussian states for discretized electromagnetic fields on a 3-manifold, using information geometry to show they minimize relative entropy under mean-helicity constraints.
motivation: To develop a statistical inference framework for magnetic helicity in discrete electromagnetism, addressing non-conservation and gauge invariance.
method: Employs Whitney discretization of the de Rham complex to separate exact, harmonic, and coexact sectors, then introduces a helicity-biased Gaussian ensemble on the reduced phase space and computes partition function, relative entropy, and Fisher information.
result: The distribution uniquely minimizes relative entropy under a prescribed mean-helicity constraint, and helicity susceptibility equals the variance of the Chern-Simons functional, controlling local distinguishability.
conclusion: The states represent conditioned inference rather than dynamical equilibrium because magnetic helicity is not conserved under unconstrained Maxwell dynamics.

title: Bridging Dependence: From Opinion Leader Influence To Standard Correlation Measures
authors: Jonas Karge
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As a cornerstone result of social choice and democracy the- ory, the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) provides probabilistic guaran- tees for the correctness of majority decisions under idealized conditions, in particular assuming that voters are statistically independent. When generalizing the original CJT, a standard approach in the literature to model dependence introduces an external opinion leader (OL) whose in- fluence affects individual voting behavior. In this paper, we take the first steps toward a unified framework for modeling dependence by translat- ing the OL model into standard correlation measures, namely covariance and correlation coefficient. These translations build conceptual bridges between different dependence models in the voting literature and facili- tate the application of existing theoretical results across frameworks.
tldr: This paper translates the opinion leader model of voter dependence into covariance and correlation measures to unify dependence models in voting theory.
motivation: The Condorcet Jury Theorem assumes voter independence, so the paper aims to bridge different models of dependence by expressing the opinion leader model in standard statistical terms.
method: The authors define translations of the opinion leader influence into covariance and correlation coefficient frameworks.
result: The translations create conceptual bridges between dependence models, enabling reuse of theoretical results across frameworks.
conclusion: This work provides a first unified framework for modeling dependence in voting, which may facilitate broader applications in social choice.

title: Collective Dressed States For Inelastic Light Scattering By Atomic Ensembles
authors: S\'ebastien Lucas, David Wilkowski, Christian Miniatura, Sergey E. Skipetrov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general dressed-state framework for computing fluorescence spectra, probe absorption spectra, and photon-photon correlations of light scattered by ensembles of [MATH] two-level atoms with arbitrary [MATH] transitions driven by intense coherent fields. The approach employs a full vectorial treatment of the electromagnetic field, handles any atomic geometries, illumination directions, and polarizations, and yields optical observables as explicit sums of Lorentzian lines whose positions, widths, and weights are directly tied to the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Lindbladian. The framework is implemented in an open-source Python package and benchmarked against exact single- and two-atom calculations. We identify geometries in which the full vectorial description is essential, and the scalar approximation fails qualitatively. Applying the method to pairs of atoms with a [MATH] transition, we show that elastic and inelastic scattered intensities collapse onto universal master curves controlled by a single collective saturation parameter built from the dominant superradiant mode, across several orders of magnitude in drive strength and interatomic distance. We identify collective phenomena that require a description beyond this single-mode picture. Extending the analysis to atoms with ground-state degeneracy, we find that most collective features carry over, while two qualitatively new effects emerge: an incoherent spontaneous Raman channel that modifies the scaling of inelastic emission, and a slow timescale in the time-delayed correlations [MATH] governed by the competition between Raman scattering and subradiant decay, controlled by a single dimensionless parameter. These results provide both physical insight and practical computational tools for engineering collective optical responses in few-atom systems such as optical tweezer arrays.
tldr: Develops a general dressed-state framework for computing light scattering observables from atomic ensembles driven by intense coherent fields, with benchmarks and discovery of universal scaling and new collective effects.
motivation: To understand and engineer collective optical responses in few-atom systems like optical tweezer arrays, including regimes where scalar approximations fail.
method: Full vectorial treatment of the electromagnetic field, expressing observables as sums of Lorentzians tied to Lindbladian eigenvalues/eigenvectors, implemented in Python and benchmarked against exact single- and two-atom calculations.
result: Identifies geometries requiring vectorial description, shows elastic and inelastic scattered intensities collapse onto universal master curves governed by a single collective saturation parameter, and finds new effects for ground-state degeneracy such as a Raman channel and a slow timescale.
conclusion: Provides physical insight and computational tools for engineering collective optical responses in few-atom systems, with potential applications in quantum optics and simulator platforms.

title: Bayesian Tracking Of A Diffusing Target In Two And Three Dimensions
authors: Adam Nahum Ewan Mcculloch
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bayesian tracking of a diffusing target monitored by a noisy distributed sensor array. Building on an earlier mapping to KPZ growth with a moving defect (or an equivalent directed polymer pinning problem) we determine the phase structure, beyond the previously-studied one-dimensional case, for both Bayes-optimal and suboptimal inference. In [MATH], theoretical analysis and numerical simulations both give a depinning transition between a successful tracking phase and a failure phase. Weak-coupling RG shows that Bayes-optimal tracking is always successful in [MATH], but failure can arise from overconfident (suboptimal) inference. In [MATH], tracking can succeed, or can fail in two distinct ways: the posterior probability distribution may delocalize (no detection), or may become sharply localized, but at the wrong position (a false detection). The two possibilities correspond to Edwards-Wilkinson or Kardar-Parisi-Zhang statistics for the log-posterior. The three phases meet at a Nishimori-like multicritical point on a Bayes-optimal line in a two-parameter phase diagram. (Model misspecification alone can drive depinning into either unpinned phase: underconfidence gives diffuse failure, while overconfidence gives localized-but-wrong failure.) We analyze the transitions between the various phases numerically and with renormalization group arguments. We show that some of these have unusual critical behavior, which the conventional [MATH] expansion fails to describe. Recent rigorous results for directed polymers indicate an alternative scenario. Many of our results, including a scaling relation for exponents at pinning transitions and results for RG flows, are relevant to other phase transitions that involve surface growth or directed polymers in 2+1D or 3+1D.
tldr: The paper analyzes Bayesian tracking of a diffusing target through mappings to KPZ growth and directed polymers, revealing phase transitions and critical behavior in inference.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits and failure modes of Bayesian tracking in noisy sensor arrays, especially the effects of model misspecification (over/underconfidence).
method: Uses theoretical mapping to KPZ growth with a moving defect (or directed polymer pinning), combined with renormalization group (RG) analysis and numerical simulations for 2D and 3D cases.
result: Identifies three distinct phases (successful tracking, diffuse failure, localized-but-wrong failure) with a Nishimori-like multicritical point, and shows that conventional RG expansions fail to describe some transitions.
conclusion: Provides scaling relations and RG flow results that are relevant beyond tracking, offering insights into phase transitions involving surface growth or directed polymers in higher dimensions.

title: Duality Between The Level Statistics Of Hermitian And non-Hermitian Random Matrices
authors: Ze Chen, Zhenyu Xiao, Yifei Liu, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random matrix theory describes complex quantum systems statistically, with symmetry as its organizing principle. We uncover an exact duality between the level statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices in the large-[MATH] (matrix size) limit. It acts class by class: the two replica partition functions, given by fermionic nonlinear [MATH] models, are related by analytic continuation. Applied to the three Wigner--Dyson classes, the duality yields the universal bulk eigenvalue pair-correlation functions of non-Hermitian random matrices. This establishes a non-Hermitian counterpart of Dyson's threefold way, organized by transposition symmetry: generic complex, complex symmetric, and complex self-dual matrices. The dissipative spectral form factors of these classes follow in closed form as well. Applied to the seven nonstandard Altland--Zirnbauer classes, the duality yields the exact spectral densities near the origin, the non-Hermitian hard-edge statistics. Most of these statistics were previously known only numerically. Exact diagonalization confirms the analytical predictions, and physical models demonstrate their universality. We expect these results to be the tip of a deeper correspondence between Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrix theory.
tldr: The paper establishes an exact duality between level statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices in the large-size limit, yielding universal spectral correlations and hard-edge statistics for various symmetry classes.
motivation: To uncover structural links between Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, potentially advancing the understanding of dissipative quantum systems through spectral statistics.
method: The authors use replica partition functions and fermionic nonlinear sigma models, applying analytic continuation to relate Hermitian and non-Hermitian classes. They derive closed-form dissipative spectral form factors and spectral densities near the origin for all relevant symmetry classes.
result: The duality reproduces known universal bulk eigenvalue correlations for the three Wigner-Dyson classes and exact hard-edge statistics for the seven nonstandard Altland-Zirnbauer classes, confirmed by exact diagonalization and physical models.
conclusion: The work provides a non-Hermitian counterpart to Dyson's threefold way and suggests a deeper correspondence between Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, but it is primarily a mathematical result with limited direct relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Optimization Landscape Geometry In Vqe For Frustrated Quantum Spin Models
authors: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'{a}k, Ivan Zelinka, Swagatam Das, Martin Beseda
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We benchmark eight classical optimizers for exact-statevector VQE calculations on a controlled hierarchy of frustrated spin models, ranging from a diagonal Ising glass to transverse-field Ising and anisotropic Heisenberg models. The benchmark includes local, stochastic-gradient, evolutionary, covariance-adaptation, and swarm-based optimization methods under matched function-evaluation budgets. To understand their performance beyond final energies, we characterize the underlying Hamiltonian--ansatz landscapes in terms of local minima, gradients, curvature, and ground-state reachability. We use simple variational circuits, from an [MATH] product-state ansatz for the diagonal model to shallow [MATH]--CNOT hardware-efficient circuits for the noncommuting models, and study how increasing circuit depth changes their expressivity, reachability, and optimization geometry. We find that optimizer performance changes substantially across the model hierarchy and is closely connected to landscape structure, while the variational gap represents a separate source of error. These results show how classical optimization, variational expressivity, and landscape geometry jointly determine VQE performance for frustrated spin models.
tldr: A benchmark of eight classical optimizers for variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) on frustrated spin models, analyzing how landscape geometry and circuit expressivity affect optimizer performance.
motivation: To understand the interplay between classical optimization, variational circuit expressivity, and Hamiltonian-ansatz landscape geometry in determining VQE performance for frustrated quantum spin models.
method: Benchmarked local, stochastic-gradient, evolutionary, covariance-adaptation, and swarm-based optimizers on exact-statevector VQE for a hierarchy of spin models (Ising, transverse-field Ising, Heisenberg) with matched function-evaluation budgets; analyzed landscapes via local minima, gradients, curvature, and ground-state reachability.
result: Optimizer performance varied substantially across the model hierarchy, closely tied to landscape structure; the variational gap was identified as a separate source of error.
conclusion: Classical optimization, variational expressivity, and landscape geometry jointly determine VQE performance for frustrated spin models, highlighting the need for model-aware optimizer selection.

title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous And Field-Induced Mechanisms Of Collective Behavior In One Dimension
authors: Weiguo Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can an artificial intelligence (AI) generate a scientific hypothesis outside a human collaborator's active hypothesis space (AHS), and can human-AI research be organized to make such breakthroughs more likely? We document such a case while proving a theorem that connects two basic organizing mechanisms of statistical physics: collective behavior arising in zero field from competing interactions and that induced or controlled by an external field. A zero-field [MATH]-vector open chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interaction functions [MATH] and [MATH] is microscopically, via a temperature-independent mapping at the Hamiltonian level, equivalent to a simpler [MATH] open chain with nearest-neighbor interaction [MATH] and axial single-spin potential [MATH] for every integer [MATH] and every system size [MATH]. The homogeneous linear specialization maps the foundational frustrated [MATH]-[MATH] model onto the canonical [MATH]-[MATH] field model---with [MATH] being the Ising, XY, and Heisenberg classical spin models, respectively. An analogous theorem holds when the continuous [MATH] spins are replaced by the [MATH]-state Potts spins with the standard Potts interaction, implying a closed-form exact solution of the [MATH]-[MATH] Potts open chain for every [MATH] and every [MATH]. The emergence of the theorems from sustained human-AI collaboration suggests that involving AI throughout a systematic research program may incubate autonomous scientific breakthroughs.
tldr: A human-AI collaboration proves a theorem connecting zero-field frustrated spin chains to field-induced models, yielding exact solutions for classical and Potts models.
motivation: To demonstrate that AI can generate hypotheses outside a human's active hypothesis space and to unify two fundamental mechanisms of collective behavior in statistical physics.
method: The theorem is proven via a temperature-independent mapping at the Hamiltonian level, showing equivalence between a frustrated spin chain with competing interactions and a simpler model with an external field. The approach is further extended to Potts spins.
result: The mapping yields exact closed-form solutions for the homogeneous [MATH]-[MATH] models (Ising, XY, Heisenberg) and the [MATH]-state Potts open chain for arbitrary system sizes and spin values.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on spontaneous vs. field-induced ordering and suggests that systematic human-AI collaboration can accelerate scientific discovery.

title: Fractal Dimension Predicts Quantum Kernel Collapse In Angle-encoded Data
authors: Ana Paula Appel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Angle-encoded quantum kernels on tabular data collapse when the feature map is wider than the intrinsic dimension of the data. We propose the correlation fractal dimension D2 as an a priori qubit budget: encode D2 coordinates chosen by FD-ASE instead of the PCA-95% width or all E attributes. On nine data sets and a statevector simulator (n= 32), a one-layer ZZ fidelity kernel at q=D2 stays geometrically alive while the same kernel at the PCA-95% width has already collapsed. The budget is map-dependent: product-state and IQP maps overshoot it; a second ZZ layer undershoots it. Packed dense-angle and re-uploading encodings still live at the fractal q, but not when PCA-95% features are stacked onto those qubits. Shrinking the angle bandwidth moves the ZZ knee later; stretching it kills the kernel earlier. On IBM Quantum (ibm_fez, 256 shots, n=8) the one-layer ZZ kernel at the fractal width matches the exact kernel (MAE 0.021); past that width both hardware and simulator have collapsed. The ceiling is a property of the map-data pair at a stated bandwidth, not of the classical table alone.
tldr: The paper proposes using the correlation fractal dimension to determine the number of qubits in angle-encoded quantum kernels, preventing kernel collapse.
motivation: Angle-encoded quantum kernels on tabular data collapse when the feature map is wider than the intrinsic dimension of the data, limiting their performance.
method: Introduce the correlation fractal dimension D2 as a qubit budget and select D2 coordinates via FD-ASE, instead of using PCA-95% width or all features.
result: On simulated and real hardware (IBM Quantum), encoding only D2 coordinates preserves kernel fidelity, while encoding PCA-95% features leads to collapse.
conclusion: Quantum kernel collapse depends on the map-data pair and bandwidth, not solely on classical data structure.

title: Dual-polarized, Mid-infrared Nonreciprocal Absorption
authors: Simo Pajovic, Yiting Zhao, Yae-Chan Lim, Ruzan Sokhoyan, Harry A. Atwater
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emission and absorption of thermal radiation are usually coupled via Kirchhoff's law or reciprocity, stated as the equality of spectral directional emissivity and absorptivity. Magneto-optical materials have recently been identified as a promising route to lifting the constraint of reciprocity, with multiple experimental demonstrations using doped InAs. However, these demonstrations have been limited to p-polarized light in the Voigt configuration, whereas thermal radiation from a blackbody is unpolarized. Therefore, to break reciprocity in both polarization channels, we design a nanophotonic, dual-polarized nonreciprocal absorber operating in the mid-infrared spectral range (11-20 [MATH]m), consisting of an a-Si photonic crystal slab on top of a doped InAs substrate described by an antisymmetric, nonreciprocal dielectric tensor under an applied magnetic field. The photonic crystal slab supports eigenmodes that couple to both s- and p-polarized light, resulting in absorption peaks that frequency shift in opposite directions for forward- and backward-propagating light[MATH]a signature of nonreciprocity in planar, subwavelength systems. We fabricate our design, then measure its room-temperature absorptance using magnetic-field-integrated absorptance spectroscopy, experimentally demonstrating nonreciprocal absorption for both polarizations. Our design is a step toward the complete control of light as heat, which could improve photonic energy conversion, thermal management, and mid-infrared optical isolation and circulation.
tldr: A nanophotonic design demonstrates dual-polarized nonreciprocal absorption in the mid-infrared by combining an a-Si photonic crystal with a magneto-optical InAs substrate.
motivation: Thermal radiation is unpolarized, yet previous nonreciprocal absorbers only operate for p-polarized light; breaking reciprocity in both polarization channels is needed for full control of light as heat.
method: The authors design a photonic crystal slab supporting modes coupled to both polarizations, fabricate it on doped InAs, and measure absorptance with magnetic-field-integrated spectroscopy.
result: They experimentally observe nonreciprocal absorption for both s- and p-polarized light, with frequency shifts reversed for forward/backward propagation.
conclusion: This work advances nonreciprocal thermal emitters/absorbers, potentially improving photonic energy conversion and mid-infrared isolation.

title: Parametric Amplification Of Continuous-variable Entangled State For Loss-tolerant Quantum Distributed Sensing
authors: Wei Wang Sijin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology exploits quantum states to achieve an estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits. In the continuous-variable (CV) regime, the squeezed state has been used to implement deterministic quantum sensing, but the quantum metrology sensitivity of this state is significantly affected by losses or detection inefficiencies, which restrict its applications. In this work, quantum distributed sensing is proposed using optical parametric amplified multimode entanglement generated from squeezed states. It is found that the sensitivity is robust to loss or detection inefficiency when large-gain optical parametric amplification (OPA) is introduced, where a two-mode Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen-entangled state and a four-mode cluster state are exploited for analysis. The quantum sensitivity is greatly improved compared to that without OPA in almost all loss scenarios. The quantum Fisher matrix is calculated for both states to obtain the optimal bound in comparison with our scheme, and it is found that even with a small or moderate OPA gain, quantum sensing can be improved compared with the traditional scheme. The states are also compared with corresponding single-mode squeezed states, finding the parameter ranges where entangled states perform better. This study provides a method for realizing large-scale quantum metrology in real-world applications despite losses or detection inefficiencies.
tldr: Proposes loss-tolerant quantum distributed sensing using continuous-variable entangled states enhanced by optical parametric amplification.
motivation: Quantum sensing with squeezed states suffers from losses; the aim is to use parametric amplification to make the scheme robust against loss and detection inefficiency.
method: Analyzes two-mode EPR-entangled and four-mode cluster states generated from squeezed states with OPA, computing quantum Fisher information to find the optimal sensitivity bounds.
result: Sensitivity is greatly improved with OPA, even at small or moderate gains, and outperforms single-mode squeezed states in many loss scenarios.
conclusion: The method enables real-world quantum metrology despite losses, providing a practical approach to large-scale quantum sensing.

title: Photonic Magnetism And Altermagnetism Without Magnetic Materials
authors: Tiancheng Zhang, Lijie Li, Zhuo Liu, Li Lei, Yi Li, Fanhao Meng, Changhao Ding, Moses C. Hong, Scott Dhuey, Jie Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetism, a fundamental property of solids arising from the collective alignment of electronic spins of magnetic atoms, has recently been expanded by the discovery of altermagnetism, a symmetry-driven phase distinct from both ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism. Initial efforts to emulate altermagnetism in photonic systems are also being pursued, primarily through the magneto-optic response of materials; however, their intrinsic frequency limitations pose challenges for extending photonic altermagnetism into the optical regime, thereby restricting their material choices and optical applications. Here, we establish a microscopic framework of photonic magnetism through group theory symmetry analysis, defining photonic counterparts of electron spin and magnetic atoms. This approach enables the realization of photonic ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and altermagnetic phases within structured optical lattices constructed by purely dielectric, nonmagnetic materials, which not only broadens the photonic magnetism concept, but also lifts the material and frequency limitations. Analytical models, numerical simulations, and experimental measurements reveal spin-momentum locking directly corresponding to their electronic analogs, showing d-, g-, and i-wave circular dichroism (CD) splitting bands at telecom wavelengths (around 1550 nm). These results demonstrate that altermagnetic order, and magnetism more broadly, can be reconstructed in photonic systems through symmetry and mode coupling alone, opening a new route towards spin-dependent light control and bosonic analogs of quantum magnetic phenomena in dielectric photonic crystals.
tldr: The paper establishes a microscopic framework for photonic magnetism, realizing photonic ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and altermagnetic phases in dielectric photonic crystals without magnetic materials, demonstrating spin-momentum locking with d-, g-, and i-wave circular dichroism at telecom wavelengths.
motivation: To emulate altermagnetism in photonic systems and overcome material and frequency limitations of magneto-optic materials, enabling optical analogies of magnetic phenomena.
method: Uses group theory symmetry analysis to define photonic analogs of electron spin and magnetic atoms, then constructs structured optical lattices of dielectric materials, with analytical models, numerical simulations, and experiments.
result: Demonstrated spin-momentum locking and d-, g-, i-wave circular dichroism at around 1550 nm, confirming photonic altermagnetic order.
conclusion: Altermagnetic order and magnetism can be reconstructed in photonic systems purely through symmetry and mode coupling, opening new routes for spin-dependent light control and bosonic analogs.

title: Ontic And Epistemic States In The Theory Of Spacetime-local Beables
authors: Nathan Argaman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bell's theorem rules out developing a locally causal theory to describe quantum phenomena. Many take this to imply that any model of quantum entanglement must employ variables (called beables by Bell) which follow nonlocal rules, even though signaling is local. The alternative is to adopt an all-at-once (block universe) approach, with beables which may depend on both past and future inputs, even though signaling is causal. Within this lenient-causality approach (a.k.a. retrocausal), simple cases of entanglement have been successfully described by locally mediated stochastic toy models, i.e.,~toy models which are local in a sense which generalizes Bell's local causality. Developing a widely applicable reformulation of quantum mechanics along these lines is a grand challenge. This work presents a general framework for such models and theories, and identifies the corresponding ontic and epistemic states. The epistemic state is closely analogous to the quantum state, yielding an explanation for the collapse of the wavefunction. In the case of the models of the framework, it is clear what the information is about. The expression for the empirically verifiable predictions of the models in terms of the ontic and epistemic states displays remarkable parallels to the Born rule. A toy-model example is discussed.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for retrocausal toy models that describe quantum entanglement using spacetime-local beables, identifying ontic and epistemic states.
motivation: Bell's theorem rules out locally causal theories, so alternatives like retrocausality are explored to account for entanglement without nonlocal effects.
method: They develop a general framework for such models, defining ontic and epistemic states, and derive predictions analogous to the Born rule.
result: They identify the epistemic state as analogous to the quantum state, explaining wavefunction collapse, and present a toy model example.
conclusion: This approach offers a potential reformulation of quantum mechanics as a locally mediated stochastic theory with retrocausality.

title: Spatio-temporal Coherent Molding And Retrieval Of Pulsed Signals In Optical Waveguides
authors: Nika Durishvili, Ramaz Khomeriki, Vakhtang Jandieri, Douglas H. Werner, Daniel Erni, Jamal Berakdar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical waveguides are key elements for high fidelity, long distance optical communications. Coupled waveguide arrays allow for higher information density, steerting the propagation direction, and for encoding information. However, due to the mixing of relative phases for short pulses containing multiple waveguide-mode frequencies, a process for retrieving an encoded input state once these signals undergo coherent propagation remains elusive. A concept is presented to extract with high fidelity the phase-encrypted input signal from spatio-temporal propagated states. As a realization, an array of coupled waveguides is suggested with the retrieval mechanism being realized by local phase shifts that comply with the identified retrieval concept. Three dimensional full-wave electromagnetic simulations for broadband optical signals in coupled dielectric waveguides confirm the validity of the scheme and the high fidelity of information retrieval pointing to potential applications, for instance in ultrafast coherent coding and decoding of information imprinted on pulse sequences.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to retrieve phase-encrypted input signals from spatio-temporal propagated states in coupled optical waveguides using local phase shifts.
motivation: Optical waveguides are crucial for high-fidelity, long-distance optical communication, but retrieving encoded input states from short pulses with multiple modes after coherent propagation is challenging.
method: They introduce a retrieval concept based on local phase shifts in an array of coupled dielectric waveguides, and validate it using 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulations.
result: Simulations demonstrate the high fidelity of information retrieval, confirming the scheme's validity.
conclusion: The approach suggests potential applications in ultrafast coherent coding and decoding of information imprinted on pulse sequences.

title: Exact Minimum Field Partition For One-Step Prediction In A Finite Five-Agent Abcw Model
authors: Takashi Inoue Shizusawa
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Which distinctions in a present state must be retained to predict a specified future exactly? We study this question on a finite reachable set of a deterministic five-agent ABCW model in which binary agent actions and strategies coevolve with a weighted directed influence field. The dataset is generated from four initial-field families and all 4,096 action-strategy initial conditions, yielding 56,536 transitions and 2,562 distinct current fields. We retain the current action and seek the coarsest field-only partition that uniquely determines the complete one-step-ahead field on every observed transition. Nine natural feature families and all 511 of their nonempty combinations provide strong approximate predictors but no exact nontrivial field compression. We therefore construct an incompatibility graph whose vertices are current fields and whose edges join fields that produce different next fields under a shared observed action. A proper 692-coloring gives a constructive upper bound. An independent anchor-action decomposition, followed by exact solution of the 50 nontrivial induced subgraphs, gives the matching lower bound. Hence the minimum number of field classes is exactly 692. This number applies only to the specified finite reachable set, field-only compression, retained current actions, one-step target, and exact-prediction requirement; it is not a universal macrostate count for ABCW systems.
tldr: This paper finds the exact minimum number of field classes (692) needed for one-step prediction in a finite five-agent ABCW model.
motivation: To determine which distinctions in a present state must be retained to exactly predict a specified future in a multi-agent system.
method: The authors construct an incompatibility graph and use graph coloring and anchor-action decomposition to derive lower and upper bounds on the number of field classes.
result: They prove that the minimum number of field classes is exactly 692 for the observed dataset.
conclusion: The exact number is specific to the given model and conditions, not a universal macrostate count for ABCW systems.

title: On The $\rho$-numerical Radius Of Rank-one Operators And Parametrized Buzano-type Inequalities
authors: Hranislav Stankovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a complex Hilbert space and [MATH]. We establish the explicit formula \[ \omega_\rho (a\otimes b)={\rho}\|a\| \|b\|+\left|1-{\rho}\right||\langle a,b\rangle|,\qquad a,b\in, \] for the [MATH]-numerical radius of rank-one operators, a unified expression interpolating between the operator norm, the numerical radius, and the spectral radius, which correspond to [MATH], and [MATH], respectively. As an application, we derive a parametrized family of Buzano-type inequalities for four vectors. We extract from it an explicit closed-form bound and, under a reality condition which is automatically satisfied in real Hilbert spaces, we determine the best bound in the family in closed form. Examples show that the resulting bounds can be strictly sharper than both the Cauchy--Schwarz and the Buzano inequality, and the classical Buzano inequality is recovered as a boundary case, which yields an alternative proof of it.
tldr: This paper is a pure mathematics contribution to operator theory, deriving explicit formulas for the rho-numerical radius of rank-one operators and new Buzano-type inequalities, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The motivation is to unify and extend classical results on numerical radius and Buzano inequalities in Hilbert spaces, providing sharper bounds and closed-form expressions.
method: The method involves analytical manipulations in complex Hilbert spaces, deriving an explicit formula for the rho-numerical radius of rank-one operators and applying it to obtain parametrized Buzano-type inequalities.
result: The result includes a unified expression for the rho-numerical radius, a parametrized family of inequalities, and closed-form bounds that can be strictly sharper than Cauchy-Schwarz and the classical Buzano inequality.
conclusion: The paper concludes with new inequalities and an alternative proof of the classical Buzano inequality, but it has no relevance to the specified research areas.

title: Extremum Seeking Control: Three Revolutions And The Road Ahead
authors: Tiago Roux Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The history of extremum seeking is not merely the history of an algorithm; it is the history of an idea. Few ideas in control engineering have demonstrated the remarkable longevity of extremum seeking control (ESC). Invented more than one hundred years ago, ESC has continually reinvented itself while remaining faithful to its original objective: enabling systems to optimize their performance without relying on accurate mathematical models. This perspective article proposes that the evolution of ESC is best understood through three scientific revolutions. The first Engineering Revolution (1922-1999) established the engineering principles of model-free optimization; the second Mathematical Revolution (2000-2010) provided the rigorous mathematical foundations that transformed ESC into a mature discipline of nonlinear control; and the third ongoing Infinite-Dimensional and Cyber-Physical Revolution (2010-present) continues to expand its scope toward delays, partial differential equations, distributed optimization, event-triggered implementations, and increasingly complex cyber-physical systems. Beyond recounting this historical evolution, we offer a personal perspective on why ESC has remained relevant across successive technological eras. We argue that its enduring influence arises because the fundamental engineering challenge has never changed: "how can a dynamical system learn to improve its own performance when the optimum is unknown?" As optimization, learning, and feedback control become increasingly intertwined, ESC appears uniquely positioned to contribute to a new generation of intelligent autonomous systems, pointing toward what may become the field's fourth scientific revolution.
tldr: This paper is a historical perspective on extremum seeking control, a model-free optimization technique in control engineering, tracing its evolution through three revolutions and speculating on future developments.
motivation: The author aims to understand why extremum seeking control has remained relevant for over a century and how it has adapted to new challenges.
method: The paper uses a historical analysis, categorizing the development of extremum seeking control into three scientific revolutions: Engineering (1922-1999), Mathematical (2000-2010), and Cyber-Physical (2010-present).
result: It identifies the three revolutions and discusses the field's expansion into distributed optimization, event-triggered control, and cyber-physical systems.
conclusion: The author argues that extremum seeking control is poised to contribute to the next generation of intelligent autonomous systems, potentially leading to a fourth revolution.

title: Entropy Stability For Diffeomorphisms Isotopic To Anosov On $\mathbb{T}^d$
authors: L. Parra, S. Ram\'irez, K. J. Vivas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the behavior of topological entropy for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms on [MATH] isotopic to a linear Anosov automorphism with indecomposable weak-stable subspace. In particular, we prove that for a class of DA maps associated with such linear systems, whose central behavior is sufficiently dominated by the expansion rate of the linear model, the topological entropy coincides with that of the linear map. Furthermore, we obtain uniqueness of equilibrium states for a class of low-oscillation potentials and, as an application, the uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also provide sufficient conditions for which ergodic measures arise as the unique equilibrium state of some continuous potential. Finally, on [MATH] we construct a dynamically coherent diffeomorphism in the same isotopy class whose topological entropy is strictly larger than that of the linear part.
tldr: This paper studies topological entropy stability for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms isotopic to Anosov automorphisms on the torus, proving entropy equality and uniqueness of equilibrium states under certain conditions.
motivation: To understand how topological entropy behaves under perturbations of Anosov systems and to characterize equilibrium states for these dynamical systems.
method: The authors analyze partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms isotopic to linear Anosov maps, using dominating expansion rates and constructing dynamically coherent examples to compare entropy.
result: They prove that for a class of DA maps with sufficiently strong central dominance, the topological entropy equals that of the linear model, and establish uniqueness of equilibrium states for potential functions with low oscillation, including the measure of maximal entropy.
conclusion: These results contribute to the theory of entropy stability in partially hyperbolic dynamical systems, extending classical results and providing conditions for equilibrium state uniqueness.

title: Capacity Achieving Torn Paper Codes
authors: Netanel Raviv Junsheng Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the torn paper channel, a codeword is cut at random locations, and the resulting error-free fragments are delivered to the decoder as an unordered multiset. Although the capacity of this channel can be achieved using random code, decoding such codes generally requires exponential time. The interleaved-pilot construction of Shomorony and Vahid embeds a De Bruijn sequence among the symbols of a shifted erasure code and aligns only fragments that are sufficiently long through global statistical uniqueness. A subsequent local-alignment scheme by Liu and Raviv employs run-length-limited constraints and exclusive all-zero markers to identify pilot positions from local structure, substantially reducing the minimum fragment length that can be aligned. We further improve the method of Liu and Raviv by replacing its fixed pilot sequence with a multilevel successive local alignment and pilot-recycling procedure. In Liu and Raviv, the pilot sequence is chosen once and must simultaneously balance the length of the pilot sequence against the ability to align short fragments. Our construction removes this limitation by reusing pilot sequences across successive decoding levels. A pilot sequence with an independent random linear code is first used to align and decode the longest fragments. The information recovered at this stage is then recycled as a larger pilot sequence for the next stage.This process is repeated over multiple levels, so that progressively shorter fragments are recovered while the length of the pilot sequence remains small. Our construction depends on choosing a series of random linear codes, and we show that for any~[MATH], there exists a choice of such codes which attains rate of at least~[MATH] below the capacity, with high probability as the block length goes to infinity. Therefore, our construction achieves the capacity of the torn-paper channel.
tldr: A multilevel pilot-recycling scheme achieves the capacity of the torn-paper channel with efficient decoding.
motivation: Capacity-achieving random codes for the torn paper channel have exponential decoding complexity, and prior pilot-based constructions limit short-fragment alignment.
method: The authors replace a fixed pilot sequence with successive decoding levels, reusing recovered information as pilots for shorter fragments, and employ random linear codes at each level.
result: For any epsilon>0, there exists a code choice attaining rate within epsilon of capacity with high probability as block length grows.
conclusion: The construction achieves capacity of the torn-paper channel while enabling efficient (polynomial-time) decoding.

title: Finite-Horizon Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman Equations With State-Dependent Diffusion In Spectral Barron Spaces
authors: Xianrui Wang Shaolin Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study high-dimensional finite-horizon Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations for controlled diffusions with uniformly elliptic, state-dependent diffusion coefficients. Motivated by the need for a rigorous analytical framework that explains neural-network approximation in high-dimensional stochastic control, we formulate the analysis in the augmented spectral Barron space. For the variable-coefficient linear equation, we construct a parametrix by freezing the second-order coefficient in the Gaussian multiplier, leading to an exact Green operator and terminal propagator without requiring small spatial variation of the diffusion coefficient. We then combine this linear theory with a semi-explicit gradient iteration for the nonlinear HJB equation and prove short-horizon convergence. The limit is a bounded classical solution and is identified with the stochastic-control value function by an It\^o verification argument. Finally, we derive a joint shallow cosine-network approximation in space and time. Taken together, our analysis connects high-dimensional stochastic control, variable-coefficient parabolic regularity, and nonlinear HJB theory with quantitative neural-network approximation, thereby providing a direct route from PDE solution analysis to neural-network complexity.
tldr: This paper provides an analytical framework in spectral Barron spaces for neural-network approximation of high-dimensional HJB equations with state-dependent diffusion.
motivation: To give a rigorous analytical basis for neural-network methods in high-dimensional stochastic control problems.
method: It constructs a parametrix for the linearized equation in augmented spectral Barron spaces, combines it with a semi-explicit gradient iteration, and derives a cosine-network approximation.
result: Short-horizon convergence to a classical solution is proven, which is identified as the value function via Itô verification.
conclusion: The work bridges stochastic control, parabolic PDEs, and neural-network complexity, but is unrelated to quantum information or quantum systems.

title: Projected Gradient Method On Hadamard Manifolds
authors: O. P. Ferreira, M. L. N. Gon\c{c}alves, A. M. Gonz\'alez, M. S. Louzeiro
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study constrained smooth optimization problems on Hadamard manifolds with closed geodesically convex feasible sets. We analyze two projected gradient schemes: one with a constant stepsize and another with a backtracking line search. The constant-stepsize scheme is analyzed under the assumption that the objective function has a Lipschitz continuous Riemannian gradient, whereas the backtracking variant does not require this assumption to establish stationarity of accumulation points. For both schemes, we prove that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is first-order stationary under the respective assumptions, without requiring compactness of the feasible set; compactness is needed only to ensure the existence of accumulation points. When the objective function has a Lipschitz continuous Riemannian gradient, we derive iteration-complexity bounds of order \(O(1/)\) for projection-based stationarity measures for both schemes, together with the corresponding \(\varepsilon\)-complexity estimates. For the backtracking scheme, the complexity analysis additionally requires the trial line-search stepsizes to be uniformly bounded away from zero. Under the same respective assumptions, the generated sequences are also asymptotically regular. Finally, we illustrate the practical performance of the methods by solving constrained Karcher mean problems on the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices.
tldr: This paper analyzes projected gradient methods for constrained optimization on Hadamard manifolds, proving convergence and complexity bounds.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical projected gradient methods to Riemannian manifolds with non-positive curvature, specifically Hadamard manifolds, where geodesic convexity holds.
method: They study two variants: constant stepsize and backtracking line search, under Lipschitz continuous Riemannian gradient assumptions, and prove stationarity of accumulation points without compactness assumptions.
result: They derive iteration-complexity bounds of order O(1/ε) for stationarity measures and show asymptotic regularity of the sequences.
conclusion: The methods are illustrated on constrained Karcher mean problems, demonstrating practical performance.

title: MaskCode: Mask Transformer For Feedback-Assisted Coding With Linear Block Codes
authors: Jonggyu Jang, Hongjae Nam, Vishrant Tripathi, David J. Love, Hyun Jong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback-based coding schemes have demonstrated substantial performance gains over today's open-loop coding schemes. Unfortunately, these gains are usually achieved in idealized settings with perfect feedback. Over the last few years, machine learning-based schemes have been shown to be promising solutions for implementing feedback-based codes, particularly when combined with short-block-length open-loop error correcting codes (ECCs) in a concatenated coding structure. However, existing ML-based feedback schemes remain agnostic to the outer code's structure, potentially misallocating feedback resources on error patterns already correctable by the outer ECC. To address this, we propose MaskCode, a Transformer-based inner feedback code for concatenated coding systems, which explicitly incorporates structural knowledge of the outer linear block code into the inner feedback encoder design via two synergistic mechanisms: 1) a soft syndrome-based input that informs the encoder about potential parity constraint violations, and 2) a code-aware attention mask derived from the Tanner graph. We further show that end-to-end training with a differentiable belief propagation (BP) decoder offers no additional gain, as MaskCode's structure-aware design already internalizes the structural knowledge of the outer code; in fact, backpropagation through the iterative BP decoder introduces gradient explosion, which degrades rather than improves performance. Extensive evaluations on BCH and LDPC outer codes demonstrate that MaskCode consistently outperforms all baselines, achieving up to 1.5 dB SNR gain.
tldr: A Transformer-based feedback code that incorporates the outer code's structural knowledge via soft syndrome input and code-aware attention masks, improving SNR gain in concatenated coding.
motivation: Existing ML-based feedback codes ignore outer code structure, leading to inefficient use of feedback resources.
method: Proposes MaskCode with soft syndrome input and attention masks derived from Tanner graphs; compares end-to-end training with BP decoder.
result: Outperforms baselines with up to 1.5 dB SNR gain on BCH and LDPC codes.
conclusion: Structure-aware design is sufficient; backpropagation through BP decoder offers no gain and causes gradient explosion.

title: Coding For Multiple Reverse-Complement And Palindromic Duplications
authors: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy

We study [MATH]-ary codes correcting [MATH] such operations performed sequentially, so a later operation may copy symbols created by an earlier one. For fixed [MATH], every length-[MATH] code [MATH] for either channel satisfies [MATH]; for fixed [MATH] and [MATH] the lower bound is [MATH].
