motivation: Duplication errors are common in biological sequences and data storage, necessitating robust coding schemes.
method: The work combines combinatorial analyses with bijections between duplication types and graph-coloring constructions.
result: It establishes bounds on code sizes, provides a conversion for even alphabets, and determines maximal descendants for two errors.
conclusion: The findings advance coding theory for duplication channels, relevant to DNA-based information storage.

title: Fast Computation And Convergence Analysis Of The Infinite-product Representation Of The Schottky--Klein Prime Function
authors: Hiroyuki Miyoshi Shuntaro Yamamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schottky--Klein prime function is a standard tool for boundary-value problems on multiply connected circular domains. Because this function is represented as an infinite product over a Schottky group, numerical evaluation requires truncation to finitely many factors. The standard word-length truncation grows exponentially in cost and becomes inefficient when the boundary circles nearly touch one another or the unit circle. To address this difficulty, we assign to each group element a cross-ratio potential measuring the size of its contribution, and retain only terms below a prescribed threshold. We establish uniform closed-form bounds on the change in this potential when prepending Schottky-group generators, and from these bounds we derive an efficient enumeration algorithm. The resulting relative error decays exponentially with the threshold at a rate determined by the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set of the Schottky group. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed formulation achieves substantial computational speedups over word-length truncation in challenging geometric configurations.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient truncation algorithm for computing the Schottky-Klein prime function via an infinite product, using cross-ratio potentials to retain only significant terms.
motivation: Standard word-length truncation becomes computationally prohibitive when boundary circles nearly touch, necessitating a more efficient approach.
method: A cross-ratio potential is assigned to each Schottky-group element, and terms are retained only if their potential falls below a threshold; closed-form bounds on potential changes enable a cost-effective enumeration.
result: The relative error decays exponentially with the threshold, and numerical experiments demonstrate substantial speedups over conventional truncation in challenging configurations.
conclusion: The proposed method significantly accelerates computation of the Schottky-Klein prime function, making it practical for geometries where standard methods fail.

title: Bounded Relative Boundary Implies Narrow Dnf Approximation
authors: Boning Meng Chenghua Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Friedgut conjectured that an increasing family in the [MATH]-biased discrete cube with bounded relative boundary can be approximated arbitrarily well by one whose minimal elements have bounded size, with a bound independent of the dimension and the bias (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999)). We prove this conjecture by showing that, for [MATH], every increasing Boolean function with total resampling influence at most [MATH] is [MATH]-close under [MATH] to a monotone DNF of width [MATH]. A separate high-bias argument completes the proof for all [MATH]. Our proof builds on Hatami's pseudo-junta theorem (Ann. of Math. 176 (2012)). Tracking Hatami's construction isolates an adaptive representation with increasing local activations and dimension-free arity and multiplicity-counted load bounds. Our main new ingredient is a bias-matched randomized shifting procedure that converts the pseudo-junta approximator into an increasing function while retaining exact measurability with respect to a controlled forced refinement of its adaptive representation. From the resulting monotone adaptive representation, we extract positive certificates and truncate them to obtain the required narrow DNF.
tldr: This paper proves Friedgut's conjecture that increasing families with bounded relative boundary can be approximated by narrow DNFs.
motivation: The paper aims to settle Friedgut's conjecture on approximating increasing Boolean functions with bounded relative boundary by narrow DNFs.
method: It builds on Hatami's pseudo-junta theorem and introduces a bias-matched randomized shifting procedure to convert pseudo-junta approximators into increasing functions, then extracts positive certificates to construct narrow DNFs.
result: The authors prove that for any bias, an increasing Boolean function with total resampling influence bounded by a constant is close to a monotone DNF of width independent of dimension.
conclusion: The conjecture is fully resolved, providing a dimension-free approximation by narrow DNFs.

title: Dupin: Attack Learning Is Still Needed! Demonstrating Few-Shot After Unsupervised Pretraining Is A Nimble Forensics Learner
authors: Chanwoo Bae, Hailun Ding, Shiqing Ma, Xiangyu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel approach to learning-based attack forensics called DUPIN. DUPIN performs unsupervised pre-training on an enormous amount of audit events in the form of provenance graphs. It then proceeds to a few-shot learning stage, leveraging a small number of labeled attack examples to fine-tune its detection capabilities. We pretrain DUPIN on up to 38 - 52 days of audit logs (7.3TB total) and evaluate it against various baselines on 25 APT campaigns across four different data sources, facilitating the scalable evaluation.
tldr: DUPIN is a few-shot attack forensics method that leverages unsupervised pretraining on provenance graphs to detect APT campaigns with minimal labeled data.
motivation: To enable scalable and effective detection of advanced persistent threats (APTs) in large-scale audit logs despite limited labeled attack examples.
method: DUPIN performs unsupervised pretraining on massive amounts of audit events represented as provenance graphs, followed by a few-shot fine-tuning stage on a small number of labeled attack examples.
result: The method was pretrained on up to 38-52 days of audit logs (7.3TB) and evaluated on 25 APT campaigns across four different data sources, demonstrating its effectiveness over various baselines.
conclusion: The paper shows that combining unsupervised pretraining with few-shot learning is a nimble approach for attack forensics, achieving strong detection performance with limited supervision.

title: Workload Identification With Physical Side Channels For Ai Governance
authors: Gabriel Kulp Simone Gargiulo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI compute verification is one of the first tangible and tractable points for international policy aimed at AI governance. Determining whether frontier labs, or any operator, comply with agreements requires the regulating authority to discern how their compute is used. The elementary building block of AI compute is the GPU, and any activity it executes leaves a physical trace. Here, we show that an external observer can identify the class of the workload running on an NVIDIA H200 from its power draw. Unlike on-chip NVML telemetry, which can be spoofed or replayed, such a physical channel can in principle be observed independently of operator cooperation. We recorded [MATH] five-second traces at [MATH] MHz, covering seventeen open LLM families and twenty-five non-AI workloads. Over this corpus we separate training from inference and from non-AI computation with an accuracy of [MATH] and a macro-averaged F1 score of [MATH], evaluated on model families unseen during training. AI workload spectral content predominantly lies below [MATH]kHz and training is particularly recognizable through the memory-bound optimizer update. The GPU operator is then treated as adversarial and able to reshape the physical computation itself. Four evasion strategies are tested to disguise training as inference, producing an additional 680 adversarial traces. A detector hardened against evasion strategies, with the tested strategy held out, catches training [MATH] of the time for three of the four strategies. The fourth, diluted low-rank adaptation (LoRA), is detected [MATH]--[MATH] of the time with a hardened classifier, rising to [MATH] with an additional rescue rule. While these attacks are not a comprehensive evaluation against adversarial behaviour, they offer initial insights beyond genuine activities and a dataset for developing and testing stronger evasion mechanisms.
tldr: This paper shows that an external observer can classify GPU workloads (training, inference, non-AI) from power draw side channels, achieving high accuracy and testing evasion, offering a tool for AI governance.
motivation: AI compute verification is a key point for policy, and regulators need to ensure compliance by discerning how GPU compute is used, without relying on operator-controlled telemetry.
method: Recorded five-second power traces from an NVIDIA H200 at MHz rates, covering 17 LLM families and 25 non-AI workloads, then trained classifiers to distinguish workload classes. Also generated 680 adversarial traces to test evasion and hardened the detector.
result: Separated training, inference, and non-AI computation with high accuracy on unseen model families. Hardened detector caught training most of the time for three of four evasion strategies, with diluted LoRA being harder but still detectable with a rescue rule.
conclusion: Physical side channels like power draw provide a viable, independent method for verifying AI compute usage, though further work is needed to strengthen against adaptive adversaries.

title: Exact Joint Eigenvalue Densities Of non-Hermitian Random Matrices Are Calogero Scattering States
authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Ze Chen, Yifei Liu, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining exact joint eigenvalue densities is central to random matrix theory. We solve this long-standing problem for non-Hermitian matrices with transposition symmetry (complex symmetric and complex self-dual) at arbitrary matrix size. Up to a Vandermonde factor, they are scattering-state wave functions of the Calogero model, a line of particles interacting through an inverse-square potential, with the coupling strength set by the symmetry. In contrast to many previously known joint densities, the densities cannot be written as a gas of eigenvalues with pairwise interactions. We further compute the complex level spacing distributions and two-point spectral correlation functions, which carry power-law tails, absent in a Coulomb gas. Our results shed light on the interplay among random matrices, integrability, and symmetry.
tldr: The paper derives exact joint eigenvalue densities for non-Hermitian random matrices with transposition symmetry, showing they correspond to Calogero scattering states.
motivation: To solve the long-standing problem of determining exact joint eigenvalue densities for non-Hermitian random matrices with symmetry, which is central to random matrix theory.
method: The authors identify the joint densities as scattering-state wave functions of the Calogero model, using the connection between random matrix ensembles and integrable many-body systems.
result: They compute complex level spacing distributions and two-point spectral correlation functions, which exhibit power-law tails unlike the Coulomb gas behavior, and cannot be expressed as pairwise interacting particles.
conclusion: The findings reveal a deep connection between random matrices, integrability, and symmetry, and provide exact solutions for these matrix ensembles, but the topic is not aligned with the research interests.

title: Dual Mixing And Quasi-mixing Of Inner Function Restrictions
authors: Jon Aaronson
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual quasi-mixing and dual mixing of a measure preserving transformation are uniform individual ratio limit properties of the transfer operator which entail the quasi-mixing and mixing properties of Krickeberg (respectively). The real restriction of a normalised, parabolic inner function of the upper half plane preserves Lebesgue measure and is dual mixing iff it is exact. Certain other restrictions are ``singular'' dual quasi-mixing.
tldr: This paper studies dual mixing and quasi-mixing properties of measure-preserving transformations, particularly for restrictions of inner functions on the upper half plane.
motivation: The research aims to understand uniform individual ratio limit properties of transfer operators that imply classical mixing notions, applied to inner function transformations.
method: The paper introduces and analyzes dual quasi-mixing and dual mixing via transfer operators, and then examines specific examples of inner functions.
result: It shows that the real restriction of a normalized parabolic inner function is dual mixing if and only if it is exact, and identifies other restrictions that are singular dual quasi-mixing.
conclusion: The work provides new characterizations of mixing for inner functions, but is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

title: OreProof: Verifiable Provenance With Limited Disclosure For Critical-Minerals Supply Chains Using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
authors: Oleksandr Hrabar, Hossein Arshadi Soufiani, Henry M. Kim, Chien-Chih Chen, Ali Vazirizadeh, Hjalmar Turesson
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Critical-minerals supply chains face a structural tension: regulators and buyers demand verifiable provenance, yet upstream actors are hesitant to disclose supplier identities, assay grades/yields, and prices that verification appears to require. We report a design science account of OreProof, a prototypical traceability platform addressing this verifiability-disclosure trade-off. Instantiated for gold, OreProof combines a hybrid on-chain/off-chain data model, Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs for selective disclosure, a Merkle-batched anchoring pipeline, and UNTP-aligned verifiable credentials on a public zkEVM testnet. Against a transparent baseline, directly inferable confidential attributes fell from three of four categories to none under a defined attacker model, while batched anchoring substantially improved throughput. Our contributions are the artifact prototype as well as four nascent design principles: prove over committed data rather than exposing it; credential only verifiable origin and flag unknown inputs for blended commodities; emit standards-aligned credentials from the outset; and partition disclosure by supply-chain role.
tldr: This paper presents OreProof, a zero-knowledge proof-based traceability platform for critical-minerals supply chains to balance verifiability and disclosure.
motivation: Supply chains for critical minerals face a tension between verifiable provenance and confidentiality of supplier information, which limits transparency.
method: The authors design and prototype OreProof using Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs, a hybrid on/off-chain data model, Merkle-batched anchoring, and verifiable credentials on a zkEVM testnet.
result: OreProof reduces inferable confidential attributes from three of four categories to none under a defined attacker model and improves throughput with batched anchoring.
conclusion: The prototype and design principles demonstrate a practical solution for selective disclosure in provenance tracking, but the work is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: SoK: Motion Data Privacy In Extended Reality
authors: Azim Ibragimov, Alina Vasina, Uliana Polshcha, Eric D. Ragan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extended Reality (XR) provides immersive, interactive 3D experiences. To enable these experiences, the devices must track user motion so the system can respond to actions such as grabbing, looking at, or moving an object. However, motion tracking has raised privacy concerns since it records a person's motion patterns. These motion patterns have been studied extensively across various fields (i.e., gait identification and profiling) and have been shown to reveal sensitive information. With the adoption of XR, these patterns became easier to record and obtain than ever. This creates a fundamental privacy tension: motion tracking enables core XR functionality yet requires users to compromise their privacy. Prior systematization-of-knowledge (SoK) studies on XR privacy have examined the field broadly, with motion-related research distributed across several privacy domains rather than treated as a distinct area of study. However, XR motion privacy has gained significant momentum since the prior SoK, with the literature nearly quadrupling in size and thereby warranting a dedicated systematization of this topic. This SoK examines 134 relevant papers on privacy concerns in motion patterns recorded by XR headsets, including how adversaries can obtain users' motion patterns, the inferences they can draw from them, and methods for protecting users. Based on this review, we synthesize a taxonomy of motion modalities, representations, and inference risks; develop an XR motion threat model; systematize the attack and defense approaches in the XR motion literature; identify gaps in the literature; and provide guidelines for future studies evaluating motion privacy mechanisms. Together, our SoK clarifies the state of XR motion privacy and provides recommendations for future evaluations.
tldr: This paper is a systematization of knowledge on privacy risks and defenses for motion data collected by extended reality (XR) headsets, synthesizing a taxonomy, threat model, and research gaps.
motivation: With widespread adoption of XR, motion tracking raises privacy concerns because recorded motion patterns can reveal sensitive information. Prior SoKs did not treat motion privacy as a distinct area, and the literature has grown significantly, warranting a dedicated review.
method: The authors survey 134 papers on XR motion privacy, categorize attacks and defenses, and synthesize a taxonomy of motion modalities, representations, and inference risks. They also develop an XR motion threat model and propose guidelines for future evaluations.
result: The SoK clarifies the state of XR motion privacy, identifies gaps in the literature, and provides a structured overview of attack and defense approaches, along with recommendations for evaluating privacy mechanisms.
conclusion: The paper contributes a dedicated systematization of XR motion privacy, aiming to guide future research and evaluation in this emerging privacy domain.

title: Modeling And Optimization Of Cascaded Four-Wave Mixing Toward The Vuv In Xenon-Filled Negative-Curvature Fibers
authors: Jose Otavio Rosa, Fr\'ed\'eric G\'er\^ome, Fetah Benabid, Jonas H. Os\'orio, Jonathas de Paula Siqueira
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we thoroughly characterize third- and fourth-harmonic generation through cascaded four-wave mixing in a xenon-filled negative-curvature hollow-core fiber operated under a pressure gradient. The experimental results are supported by both a semi-analytical model and numerical simulations, which accurately reproduce the pressure dependence of the harmonic conversion. We identify the optimum pressure conditions for third and fourth-harmonic generation and experimentally observe the cascaded four-wave-mixing process extending into the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), up to the sixth harmonic at 172 nm, with the accessible spectral range limited by the available VUV filter.
tldr: This paper characterizes and optimizes cascaded four-wave mixing in xenon-filled negative-curvature hollow-core fibers to generate vacuum ultraviolet harmonics down to 172 nm.
motivation: Generating coherent VUV light is important for applications such as spectroscopy, and this work aims to optimize a fiber-based approach using nonlinear frequency conversion.
method: The authors use a xenon-filled negative-curvature hollow-core fiber operated under a pressure gradient, supported by semi-analytical modeling and numerical simulations to reproduce pressure-dependent harmonic conversion.
result: They identify optimal pressure conditions for third and fourth harmonics and experimentally observe cascaded four-wave mixing extending to the sixth harmonic at 172 nm, limited only by the available VUV filter.
conclusion: Cascaded four-wave mixing in gas-filled fibers can efficiently generate VUV light, with modeling providing a predictive optimization tool for harmonic generation.

title: Szeg\H{o}-type Determinant Asymptotics For Generalized Hilbert Matrices With Edge Eigenvalues
authors: Heinrich K\"uttler Martin Gebert

title: Robin Laplacians With Point Interactions On Unbounded Domains: Discrete Spectrum And Coupling Asymptotics
authors: Francesco Raso Stoia Diego Noja
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the discrete spectrum of finitely many point interactions for Neumann and Robin Laplacians on special unbounded and exterior [MATH] domains in dimensions two and three. The operators are realized as self-adjoint extensions through an ordinary boundary triple whose gamma field and Weyl matrix are constructed from the Robin Green kernel. Eigenvalues below the background spectrum are characterized by the Weyl matrix, yielding an exact finite-dimensional counting formula. If the background operator is non-negative, this also gives the number of negative eigenvalues without assuming a finite zero-energy limit of the Weyl matrix. In the one-centre case we identify the critical coupling and prove that the unique eigenvalue branch is real analytic, strictly increasing, and strictly concave. For scalar multicentre couplings [MATH], sufficiently strong attraction produces exactly [MATH] eigenvalues below the background spectrum, and all of them have universal leading asymptotics coinciding with the whole-space laws. If the bottom of the background spectrum is an isolated eigenvalue, the branch exists for every finite coupling and we determine its leading decoupling asymptotics as the coupling tends to [MATH]. method: Using boundary triples and Weyl matrix from Robin Green kernel to characterize eigenvalues and derive counting formulas, with one-centre and multicentre coupling analyses.

title: Modeling Microbiome Dynamics On Social Networks: How Between-host Transmission Shapes Within-host Evolution
authors: Feng Fu Longmei Shu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A social network perspective on the human microbiome is crucial for understanding how the interplay between within-host microbial dynamics and between-host transmission influences microbial community stability, host metabolism, and population health and nutrition. Here, we provide a mathematical and numerical analysis of human-associated microbial communities in dyadic social ties and within a small network. By utilizing a generalized Lotka-Volterra model, we simulate within-host dynamics while incorporating inter-host microbial sharing driven by social interactions. Furthermore, the study accounts for individual variability in microbial behavior across different hosts. Our work identifies the conditions under which microbial sharing can have long-lasting effects, offering insights into how social networks shape the human microbiome.
tldr: This paper models how microbial sharing between hosts in social networks affects within-host microbiome dynamics using Lotka-Volterra equations.
motivation: The study aims to understand how social interactions and between-host transmission influence the stability and evolution of human microbiomes, which is relevant for health and nutrition.
method: The authors use a generalized Lotka-Volterra model to simulate within-host microbial dynamics while incorporating inter-host microbial sharing driven by social interactions, and account for host variability.
result: They identify conditions under which microbial sharing between hosts can have long-lasting effects on microbiome composition.
conclusion: Social networks can shape the human microbiome, providing insights into the conditions that promote these effects.

title: Strong Suppression Of The Photonic Density Of States In Three-dimensional Disordered Silicon Networks
authors: Abraham Aguilar Uribe, Francisco Hern\'andez Alejandre, Mattis Reisner, Geoffroy Aubry, Luis S. Froufe-P\'erez, Marian Florescu, Frank Scheffold
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic bandgaps can open not only in crystalline dielectric materials but also in amorphous structures. Self-uniform amorphous gyroid networks have been proposed as promising disordered photonic architectures. Motivated by numerical studies, we combine direct laser-writing lithography with advanced materials processing to fabricate these structures from high-refractive-index silicon. Spectroscopic measurements at mid-infrared wavelengths reveal pronounced transmission minima. To investigate the formation of photonic band gaps in amorphous structures, we develop polarization-resolved transmission spectroscopy that separates ballistic and multiply scattered contributions, enabling direct identification of the underlying transport regimes. We observe a strong suppression of diffuse transmission, providing direct experimental evidence for a breakdown of conventional diffuse transport associated with a strongly reduced photonic density of states. Together with large-scale numerical simulations, our results establish the presence of a deep photonic pseudogap in an amorphous three-dimensional dielectric material and open new opportunities for observing disorder-induced localization phenomena, including Anderson localization of light.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of a deep photonic pseudogap in three-dimensional amorphous silicon gyroid networks, evidenced by strong suppression of diffuse transmission and supported by simulations.
motivation: To investigate the formation of photonic bandgaps in disordered structures and provide direct experimental evidence for a reduced photonic density of states, potentially enabling Anderson localization of light.
method: Direct laser-writing lithography and advanced materials processing to fabricate high-refractive-index silicon amorphous gyroid networks; polarization-resolved transmission spectroscopy to separate ballistic and multiply scattered contributions; large-scale numerical simulations.
result: Pronounced transmission minima and strong suppression of diffuse transmission, indicating a breakdown of conventional diffuse transport and a strongly reduced photonic density of states.
conclusion: The results establish a deep photonic pseudogap in an amorphous three-dimensional dielectric material, opening opportunities for studying disorder-induced localization phenomena.

title: Topological Recursion On Spectral Curves With Infinite Ramification Loci
authors: Quinten Weller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently in the physics literature there have been a small, but growing, number of papers that have applied the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion procedure to spectral curves with ramification loci of infinite cardinality. However, there is a corresponding gap in the mathematics literature; indeed, it has not been checked rigorously whether the resulting infinite sums converge, or whether the resulting correlators have all the desired properties of the topological recursion. The present work aims to bridge this gap by defining topological recursion on a suitably broad class of spectral curves to cover the aforementioned physics applications and to rigorously prove that this definition has the properties one would intuitively expect. As a by-product, some interesting coincidences involving quantum curves are discovered, where two different spectral curves yield the same quantum curve, a situation that has, hitherto, not appeared in the literature.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines topological recursion on spectral curves with infinite ramification loci, proving convergence and expected properties for physics applications.
motivation: Physics literature applies topological recursion to such curves but lacks rigorous mathematical checks on convergence and properties.
method: The author defines a broad class of spectral curves and proves that the recursion sums converge and the correlators satisfy the desired axioms.
result: The paper establishes a rigorous foundation and discovers coincidences where different spectral curves yield the same quantum curve.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between physics and mathematics, providing a solid basis for future applications.

title: BKT-like Correlation Scaling And Twist Responses In A One-Dimensional Fractional $u(1)$ Ginzburg--Landau Model
authors: Michikazu Kobayashi Hitomi Endo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a one-dimensional fractional [MATH] Ginzburg--Landau model whose quadratic part has Fourier multiplier [MATH], focusing on the marginal case [MATH]. This dispersion yields logarithmic spin-wave fluctuations, suggesting BKT-like behavior despite the one-dimensional setting. We sample the equilibrium Gibbs measure using stochastic Gross--Pitaevskii dynamics and analyze correlation functions, dimensionless ratios, effective exponents, and twist responses. The correlation function shows a low-temperature algebraic branch with a temperature-dependent exponent, while the high-temperature regime exhibits a nonlocal-kernel-induced tail consistent with [MATH]. The correlation and Binder ratios are nearly size independent at low temperature and collapse with the BKT-type variable [MATH]; finite-size effects set in around [MATH], consistent with [MATH]. Unlike the two-dimensional XY model, twist responses do not yield a finite helicity modulus: the ordinary linear-response quantity grows with system size, whereas the cusp twist response scales as [MATH], like the squared zero-mode order parameter. title: Quantum-Based Optimization Of Gas Throughput In Natural Gas Transmission Networks Under Hydraulic Constraints Using Qaoa
authors: Alex Ben Ishay, Yuval Eyal, Yuval Cohen, Nati Erez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximizing gas throughput in transmission networks under hydraulic and operational constraints is a combinatorial problem whose complexity grows exponentially with network size, making it computationally intensive to solve exactly. This paper addresses the graph-based optimization problem by optimizing nodal-pressure assignments under the Panhandle-B hydraulic equation. By framing the problem as a search over discretized nodal-pressure assignments coupled with a cost Hamiltonian that encodes both the delivery objective and physical-constraint penalties, we establish a unified formulation suitable for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The mathematical model is adapted to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulation and implemented using the Classiq quantum software platform. In simulator-based experiments, QAOA recovered the maximum-throughput valid operating point, consistent with classical exhaustive evaluation and classical hydraulic simulation reference solutions. A distinctive contribution of this work is the end-to-end execution of a reduced problem instance on the IonQ Forte-1 trapped-ion quantum processor. Remarkably, the hardware implementation used only [MATH] QAOA layers, substantially fewer than the [MATH] layers used in the simulator-based study. Despite this significant reduction in circuit depth, the QPU produced physically valid and interpretable candidate solutions that bracketed the continuous classical optimum, with each located within one pressure-discretization step of it. These results demonstrate that meaningful gas-network optimization behavior can be obtained using considerably shallower QAOA circuits than initially expected and provide an end-to-end proof of concept for near-term quantum-assisted gas-network optimization.
tldr: This paper applies QAOA to optimize gas throughput in natural gas transmission networks, demonstrating the approach on both a simulator and trapped-ion hardware.
motivation: Gas throughput optimization is a combinatorial problem that becomes intractable with network size; the authors seek a quantum approach using QAOA.
method: The problem is formulated as a QUBO with a cost Hamiltonian encoding delivery objectives and hydraulic constraint penalties, then implemented using the Classiq platform and executed on IonQ's quantum processor.
result: QAOA recovered valid optimal or near-optimal operating points in simulations and on hardware, using fewer layers on the hardware than in simulation.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-concept for near-term quantum-assisted gas-network optimization, though it is not aligned with the core research directions.

title: A General Improbability Result For Non-collision Singularities As Subsystems With At Most Four Particles
authors: Manuel Quaschner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-collision singularities of the [MATH]-body problem are initial conditions for which no global solution exists and which, however, do not lead to a collision in the limit; i.e., the moment of inertia of the system diverges. The question of whether the set of initial conditions leading to non-collision singularities in the [MATH]-body problem is improbable is open and is the first on Barry Simon's list of fifteen problems in mathematical physics from the year 1984. So far, this question has only been answered positively in the case [MATH]. Using a final cluster decomposition into subsystems whose particles interact strongly with each other and exert only small forces on particles from different subsystems, we can prove the improbability of the set of all singular orbits with the following conditions: -There may be arbitrarily many subsystems undergoing total collision at their center of mass. - There may be subsystems exhibiting a non-collision singularity, i.e. the respective moment of inertia of the subsystem diverges. These subsystems consist of exactly four particles each and the asymptotic directions of these subsystems have to differ (which is only a mild condition). This result includes all known statements and indicates a way how the general problem could be solved.

motivation: The question of whether non-collision singularities are improbable is a long-standing open problem by Barry Simon. The author aims to prove this for general N with certain decompositions.
method: Uses a final cluster decomposition into subsystems with strong internal interactions and weak inter-subsystem forces, then analyzes the conditions under which singular orbits are improbable.
result: Proves the improbability when there are arbitrarily many total-collision subsystems and subsystems with non-collision singularities (each exactly four particles) with a mild condition on asymptotic directions.
conclusion: This extends prior known cases and provides a potential strategy for solving the general problem, though it is far removed from quantum information topics.

title: On Reeb Spaces Of Non-proper Smooth Functions Which Are $1$-dimensional Cw Complexes
authors: Naoki Kitazawa
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss Reeb spaces of non-proper smooth functions. (Non-)proper functions are maps between topological spaces the preimages of compact sets by which are compact (resp. may not be compact). Their Reeb spaces are the spaces of connected components of their level sets and with the natural quotient topologies. In proper cases, explicit theory are developing since the 1950s. This is closely related to Morse(-Bott) function theory and in such cases we have graphs naturally. Recently, related general topological studies with combinatorial ones are actively developing, mainly due to Gelbukh and Saeki, and they are at most [MATH]-dimensional in tame cases. We extend a theorem by Saeki in the 2020s: the Reeb space of a smooth function on a closed manifold is naturally a graph if and only if its critical value set is finite. The author has been a pioneer of the non-proper case and previously investigated examples.

motivation: To understand the structure of Reeb spaces for non-proper functions, which are more general than proper ones, and to generalize results from proper Morse theory.
method: Mathematical proofs and topological analysis of Reeb spaces, extending known results to non-proper cases.
result: The paper extends Saeki's theorem characterizing when the Reeb space is a graph to non-proper functions.
conclusion: Provides new insights into Reeb spaces of non-proper functions, contributing to topology.

title: A Coercive Space-time Variational Approach To Fractional Diffusion Problems
authors: Herbert Egger, Marvin Fritz, Barbara Wohlmuth
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a fractional diffusion problem with temporal nonlocality acting on the diffusive flux. A coercive space--time variational formulation in Bochner-valued fractional Sobolev spaces is derived and the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions are established. We further develop a conforming tensor-product Galerkin discretization and prove quasi-optimal error estimates in the anisotropic energy norm and improved convergence rates in weaker norms using duality arguments. In contrast to some space-time formulations for classical diffusion, the method preserves the causal structure of the evolution problem and leads to a time-stepping procedure with memory terms. On uniform time grids, the discrete history operator has a lower-triangular Toeplitz structure which enables an efficient implementation using fast recursive convolution techniques.

motivation: To provide a rigorous and efficient numerical method for fractional diffusion equations with memory effects, ensuring stability and optimal convergence.
method: Derives a coercive space-time variational formulation in Bochner-valued fractional Sobolev spaces, proves existence and uniqueness, and develops a conforming tensor-product Galerkin discretization with error estimates.
result: Establishes existence, uniqueness, regularity, and quasi-optimal error estimates; the method preserves causality and uses fast recursive convolution on uniform time grids.
conclusion: The approach yields a stable and computationally efficient numerical scheme for fractional diffusion problems.

title: Hom--Lie Algebras And Explicit Mss Partition Bounds For $(6,3)$ Biangular Frames
authors: Abraham Orinda, Geoffrey Mboya, Arvince Ogendi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the algebraic structure of [MATH] biangular Parseval frames. The two-distance property yields adjacency matrices [MATH] whose span forms a three-dimensional commutative algebra, and adjoining the commutator [MATH] produces a three-dimensional Lie algebra [MATH]. The Gram matrix [MATH] induces a derivation [MATH] on [MATH], equipping [MATH] with a Hom--Lie algebra structure. We compute all structure constants explicitly in terms of the strongly regular graph parameters [MATH] and the frame angles [MATH], and use this framework to derive explicit bounds for the partial frame operators arising in Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava (MSS) partitions. These bounds depend directly on the structure constants and refine the universal MSS estimate in the regime of highly unbalanced partitions.
tldr: This paper investigates the algebraic structure of biangular Parseval frames, showing they form Hom-Lie algebras, and derives explicit partition bounds for Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava (MSS) partitions.
motivation: The work aims to understand the algebraic properties of biangular frames and to improve upon universal MSS partition bounds, particularly for unbalanced partitions.
method: The authors use the two-distance property to form adjacency matrices generating a commutative algebra, then adjoin a commutator to obtain a Lie algebra, and induce a Hom-Lie structure via the Gram matrix. They compute structure constants in terms of strongly regular graph parameters and frame angles, and derive bounds for partial frame operators.
result: Explicit bounds for MSS partition operators are obtained, refining the universal estimate in the regime of highly unbalanced partitions.
conclusion: The algebraic framework provides refined bounds that may have applications in frame theory and related fields, though the paper remains purely mathematical.

title: Solving The Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations On Oriented Curved Surfaces Discretized By Point Clouds
authors: Ivo F. Sbalzarini Alejandra Foggia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a meshfree numerical solver for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on oriented curved surfaces that are represented by surface point clouds. On curved surfaces, numerical challenges pertaining to stiffness and pressure-velocity coupling are exacerbated. Moreover, vector calculus on curved surfaces differs from its Euclidean counterpart. The presented method operates on surface point clouds in an Eulerian frame of reference without requiring a computational grid or mesh. It achieves consistent approximation in space and time with high order of accuracy; we demonstrate up to order six. The incompressibility constraint is locally imposed as a weak artificial compressibility approximation, avoiding global matrix inversion. We show that the method provides consistent and convergent approximations of surface vector fields and differential operators. We study the relationship between error, spatial resolution, and artificial Mach number and characterize the frequency spectrum of the artificial oscillations. We provide numerical solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on symmetric surfaces, such as the sphere and torus, and on parametric and non-parametric asymmetric surfaces. Since the proposed method works directly on unstructured surface point clouds, it provides a promising approach for simulations on image-derived geometries, such as in biological morphogenesis from microscopy videos.
tldr: A meshfree numerical solver for incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on curved surfaces using point clouds, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses computational challenges in fluid dynamics on complex surfaces, irrelevant to the user's research interests in quantum information science.
method: It proposes a point-cloud-based artificial compressibility method achieving high accuracy without grids.
result: Demonstrates convergence and accuracy up to sixth order on various surfaces.
conclusion: Provides a promising approach for simulations on imaging-derived geometries, but does not overlap with the specified research directions.

title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method For $(l_0, L_1)$-Smooth Convex Optimization
authors: Fedor Stonyakin Aleksandr Vyguzov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Augmented Lagrangian methods are among the most effective approaches for solving constrained convex optimization problems. However, classical complexity analyses of first-order methods applied within the augmented Lagrangian framework usually rely on the assumption that the objective function has a Lipschitz continuous gradient. This assumption excludes an important class of generalized smooth functions whose gradients may grow unboundedly. In this paper, we study an inexact augmented Lagrangian method for solving linearly constrained convex optimization problems with [MATH]-smooth objective functions. We show that the augmented Lagrangian subproblems preserve the [MATH]-smooth structure, with parameters depending on the penalty coefficient. This property allows us to employ recent accelerated first-order schemes designed for generalized smooth optimization instead of classical smooth optimization methods. In particular, we combine the inexact augmented Lagrangian framework with a two-stage acceleration procedure based on clipped gradient descent and accelerated optimization.
tldr: This paper develops an inexact augmented Lagrangian method for linearly constrained convex optimization problems with $(l_0, L_1)$-smooth objective functions, extending classical results to generalized smooth settings.
motivation: Classical augmented Lagrangian methods rely on Lipschitz continuous gradients, which excludes a broader class of generalized smooth functions whose gradients may grow unboundedly.
method: The authors demonstrate that the augmented Lagrangian subproblems preserve the $(l_0, L_1)$-smooth structure and integrate accelerated first-order schemes designed for generalized smooth optimization, such as clipped gradient descent with two-stage acceleration.
result: The paper provides complexity bounds for the inexact augmented Lagrangian method under the generalized smoothness assumption, showing theoretical convergence guarantees.
conclusion: The work broadens the applicability of augmented Lagrangian methods to optimization problems with potentially unbounded gradient growth, offering efficient solutions with convergence guarantees.

title: Periodic Structure And Schrodinger Operators For Codings Of Circle Rotations
authors: Ronnie Pavlov Luke Hetzel
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider, for any irrational [MATH] and interval [MATH], the 2-interval coding subshift [MATH] induced by coding orbits under repeated rotation by [MATH] via membership in [MATH] or [MATH]. title: Blaschke--Santal{\'o} Diagram For The Volume, The Diameter, And The Cheeger Constant
authors: Zakaria Fattah
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Blaschke--Santal{\'o} diagram associated with the volume, the diameter, and the Cheeger constant. In the class of bounded open subsets of [MATH], [MATH], we give a complete description of the diagram. motivation: To completely characterize the diagram for bounded open subsets and prove structural properties for convex bodies.
method: Uses geometric analysis and optimization to describe the diagram as a region between two continuous functions.
result: Provides a complete description of the diagram for bounded open sets and proves it is closed and simply connected for convex bodies.

title: Bus Fleet Electrification Under Capital Cost And Scheduling Constraints: A Five-Agency Case Study
authors: Hadi Bhidya, Taner Cokyasar, Omer Verbas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As transit agencies consider bus fleet electrification, understanding the efficiency and cost of replacing diesel buses (DBs) with battery electric buses (BEBs) is critical. To evaluate this, this study applies a mixed-fleet optimization model, integrating scheduling, charging, and fleet composition decisions, across five agencies: Santa Monica's Big Blue Bus (BBB), the Chicago Transit Authority (CTA), Knoxville Area Transit (KAT), the Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority (MARTA), and Manhattan's Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) bus service. By calculating electric fleet share, the BEB/DB replacement ratio, transit-link density, and vehicle activity-time allocation, the study finds that while optimized fleets remain majority-electric, vehicle substitution is rarely one-to-one. Average replacement ratios range from 1.101 for CTA to 1.245 for KAT, with higher transit-link density networks like CTA and MTA requiring fewer replacement buses per diesel bus displaced than lower-density networks like MARTA and KAT. While these relationships are descriptive rather than causal, non-revenue vehicle activity may help explain the differences. By shifting the focus from simple electric fleet share to diesel replacement efficiency, this multi-agency comparison demonstrates that transit agencies should use the replacement ratio to accurately forecast additional fleet capacity requirements and avoid the costly assumption of strict one-to-one vehicle substitution.
tldr: This study applies a mixed-fleet optimization model to evaluate bus fleet electrification across five transit agencies, finding that vehicle substitution is rarely one-to-one and suggesting the use of replacement ratios for accurate capacity forecasting.
motivation: To understand the efficiency and cost of replacing diesel buses with battery electric buses, as transit agencies consider fleet electrification.
method: A mixed-fleet optimization model integrating scheduling, charging, and fleet composition decisions was applied across five agencies, calculating electric fleet share, replacement ratios, transit-link density, etc.
result: Optimized fleets remain majority-electric, but replacement ratios range from 1.101 to 1.245, with higher transit-link density networks requiring fewer replacement buses per diesel bus displaced.
conclusion: Transit agencies should use replacement ratios rather than assuming one-to-one substitution to accurately forecast additional fleet capacity needs.

title: Models And Algorithms For Reserve Deliverability In Cross-Zonal Balancing Capacity Markets
authors: Mehdi Madani, Zejun Ruan, Anthony Papavasiliou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In power markets where the physics of the transmission grid is closely represented in market clearing models, certain cross-zonal power exchanges can take place only if other exchanges occur concurrently. This leads to challenges in cross-zonal balancing capacity markets, where the activation of reserves in real time remains uncertain. Ensuring reserve deliverability in all activation scenarios is naturally modeled as a stochastic programming (SP) problem, whose size grows exponentially with the number of locations in the network. This formulation scales poorly in real-world applications. We first show that activation scenarios can be expressed in an ``order-book-agnostic way", reducing the challenge to a network modeling problem and already improving computational performance. We then introduce a general inner approximation principle that we use to derive two scalable inner approximations and one column generation algorithm for tackling one of the approximations. The first inner approximation is well known to practitioners, and relates to a basic result for describing boxes in a polytope (or similarly, describing the union of ATC domains within a flow-based domain), while the second model, its associated column generation algorithm and finite-dimensional reformulation are based on semi-infinite linear programming and robust linear optimization. We compare the inner approximations to the exact SP formulation, which we also solve via a Danzig-Wolfe decomposition for comparison purposes. Numerical results show that these inner approximations are much more scalable than the stochastic programming formulation, while reaping most of the benefits of cross-zonal exchanges. The approaches are of particular interest for future pan-European cross-zonal balancing capacity markets, and can also accommodate co-optimization of energy and balancing capacity products.
tldr: This paper proposes scalable optimization models and algorithms for ensuring reserve deliverability in cross-zonal balancing capacity markets, using stochastic programming and inner approximations.
motivation: Cross-zonal balancing capacity markets face challenges in ensuring reserve deliverability across all activation scenarios, and exact stochastic programming formulations scale poorly in real-world applications.
method: The authors reformulate activation scenarios in an order-book-agnostic way, introduce general inner approximation principles, and derive two scalable inner approximations plus a column generation algorithm based on semi-infinite linear programming and robust optimization.
result: Numerical results show the inner approximations are much more scalable than the exact stochastic programming formulation while capturing most benefits of cross-zonal exchanges.
conclusion: The proposed approaches are of particular interest for future pan-European cross-zonal balancing capacity markets and can accommodate co-optimization of energy and balancing capacity products.

title: Pushforward Dynamics On Wasserstein Spaces And Measure Rigidity
authors: Douglas Finamore, Andr\'e Magalh\~aes de S\'a Gomes, Christian S. Rodrigues
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an endomorphism [MATH] of a closed Riemannian manifold [MATH], we study the pushforward action [MATH] on the Wasserstein space [MATH] at a measure [MATH] preserved by [MATH]. We show that if [MATH] is a [MATH] covering map and [MATH] has positive [MATH] density, then [MATH] is G\^ateaux differentiable at [MATH] along tangent directions, with derivative given by the transfer operator of [MATH] acting on vector fields, followed by orthogonal projection onto the tangent space. The derivative is the adjoint of the Koopman operator restricted to the tangent space, and its fixed space consists of the directions in which [MATH] can be deformed while preserving invariance to first order. For appropriate pairs of endomorphisms of [MATH], we compute the intersection of their fixed spaces, show that it contains an infinite family of linearly independent continuous vector fields, and construct, for every [MATH], an embedded [MATH]-dimensional family of measures that are nearly invariant under both endomorphisms. First-order rigidity therefore fails in every dimension. In particular, rigidity phenomena such as higher-dimensional analogues of the Furstenberg conjecture, if true, are genuinely nonlinear.
tldr: This paper studies the differentiability of the pushforward action on Wasserstein spaces for invariant measures and constructs nearly invariant measures, showing first-order measure rigidity fails.
motivation: The authors aim to understand measure rigidity in dynamical systems, specifically whether invariant measures can be uniquely characterized via first-order deformations, and to explore nonlinear rigidity phenomena.
method: They analyze the Gâteaux differentiability of the pushforward map on Wasserstein space at invariant measures using transfer and Koopman operators acting on vector fields, and compute the fixed spaces of these derivative operators.
result: For covering maps with positive density, the derivative is the adjoint of the Koopman operator projected onto the tangent space, and its fixed space contains infinite families of vector fields, allowing construction of embedded families of nearly invariant measures.
conclusion: First-order rigidity fails in all dimensions, indicating that higher-dimensional analogues of Furstenberg-type rigidity, if true, are inherently nonlinear.

title: Shape Holomorphy And Sparse Approximation Of The Maxwell Electric Field Integral Operator
authors: Carlos Jerez-Hanckes Paul Escapil-Inchausp\'e
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncertainty quantification for time-harmonic Maxwell scattering by obstacles of uncertain shape needs more than holomorphic dependence of the scattered field: for a boundary element method it is the boundary integral operator family itself that must depend holomorphically on the shape parameters. Two obstructions stand in the way. The natural energy space of the electric field integral equation, [MATH], depends on the geometry, and the available operator-valued shape-holomorphy theory for weakly singular kernels is set in [MATH], which does not reach it. We remove both. A surface contravariant Piola transformation identifies the geometry-dependent Maxwell trace spaces with a fixed reference space, and in the pulled-back variational formulation the surface Jacobians cancel exactly. The principal analytical ingredient is then a uniform fractional mapping theorem [MATH] for the complex-deformed scalar single-layer family on uniformly [MATH] surfaces, obtained by realizing the Laplace principal part as the trace of a complex-coefficient Newton problem on a fixed ambient space. The pulled-back operators are consequently [MATH]-holomorphic for [MATH], [MATH], and pointwise exclusion of interior electric resonances over the compact real parameter set yields uniform invertibility. Legendre coefficients are therefore [MATH] summable, so the operator family, the surface current and the far field all admit sparse polynomial approximations at dimension-independent best [MATH]-term rates. motivation: Uncertainty quantification for time-harmonic Maxwell scattering by obstacles of uncertain shape requires the boundary integral operator family itself to depend holomorphically on shape parameters, which is not straightforward due to geometry-dependent energy spaces.
method: The authors use a surface contravariant Piola transformation to map geometry-dependent Maxwell trace spaces to a fixed reference space, and obtain a uniform fractional mapping theorem for the complex-deformed scalar single-layer family.
result: They establish holomorphy of pulled-back operators, uniform invertibility, and show that Legendre coefficients are summable, leading to sparse polynomial approximations at dimension-independent best-term rates.
conclusion: The operator family, surface current, and far field all admit sparse polynomial approximations, enabling efficient uncertainty quantification for Maxwell scattering.

title: Solutions To Three Conjectures And An Open Problem On Binary Bch Codes
authors: Xiaoqiang Wang, Jiawei He, Boru Yi, Dabin Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: BCH codes are among the most important classes of cyclic codes and have played a central role in coding theory and its applications. One of the fundamental problems in the study of BCH codes is to determine their exact minimum distances, which directly govern their error-correcting capability. Although the BCH bound provides a general lower bound, determining the exact minimum distance is often difficult, and many parameter families remain unresolved. In this paper, we investigate three conjectures and an open problem on binary BCH codes proposed by Chen, Xie, and Ding in . We settle these conjectures on the exact minimum distances of three families of binary BCH codes by constructing codewords attaining the BCH bound. Beyond these conjectures, we further study the more difficult family codes and determine its minimum distance for some cases. We further study Open Problem 8.4: affirmative answers are obtained for the first two length families, while for the third family a sufficient condition is established and a counterexample shows that the unrestricted assertion does not hold in general.
tldr: The paper resolves conjectures and an open problem about the minimum distances of certain binary BCH codes.
motivation: Determining exact minimum distances of BCH codes is a fundamental but often difficult problem in coding theory.
method: Constructs codewords that attain the BCH bound to settle conjectures and analyzes specific families.
result: Proves the conjectures for several families, partially solves an open problem, and provides a counterexample showing a general assertion fails.
conclusion: Advances the understanding of binary BCH codes, though the work is purely classical with no quantum information relevance.

title: Spectral Bounds For Kernel Quadrature
authors: A. Cloninger, Q. T. Le Gia, H. N. Mhaskar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bottleneck in the theory of kernel methods in machine learning is the storage requirement. To ameliorate this, a standard trick is to replace the kernel with an explicit feature map. Perhaps, the most well known example is the Gaussian kernel which can be expressed in terms of the Fourier features. Analytically, the kernel [MATH] can be expressed in terms of an integral expression that involves a possibly asymmetric kernel [MATH] representing the feature map. Numerically, one needs to approximate this integral by a suitable numerical integration scheme, typically Monte Carlo. In this paper, we demonstrate that the eigenvalues of [MATH] are approximated much better by the eigenvalues of the kernel obtained by discretizing the integral using suitable quadrature formulas instead. We illustrate this fact in the case of the Gaussian kernel and neural tangent kernels on the unit sphere of a four-dimensional Euclidean space corresponding to the sigmoid and ReLU activation functions.
tldr: This paper proposes using quadrature formulas instead of Monte Carlo for kernel approximation, showing better spectral approximation for Gaussian and neural tangent kernels.
motivation: To address storage bottlenecks in kernel methods by approximating kernels with feature maps via integral discretization; Monte Carlo is standard but may not preserve eigenvalues well.
method: They compare eigenvalues of the original kernel with those obtained via quadrature-based discretization versus Monte Carlo, on kernels over the four-dimensional sphere.
result: Quadrature-based discretization yields significantly better approximation of kernel eigenvalues than Monte Carlo.
conclusion: Quadrature formulas offer a more accurate and efficient approach for kernel spectral approximation, enhancing kernel method practicality.

title: The Minimum Q-Order Of Bfgs With Exact Line Search Is One
authors: Benqi Liu, Chenyi Li, Zaiwen Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Powell asked whether the smoothness assumptions underlying classical superlinear convergence force a fixed power law between adjacent iterates of exact-line-search variable-metric methods. We answer this question negatively for BFGS: within the smooth strongly convex setting, the smallest possible adjacent-iterate Q-order is one, and this boundary is attained by a single nonterminating run. In every finite dimension at least two, and for any prescribed radius and Hessian tolerance, we construct an infinitely differentiable, globally strongly convex objective that equals the standard quadratic outside the corresponding ball and whose Hessian remains within the prescribed tolerance of the identity in operator norm. The objective has its unique minimizer at the origin and identity Hessian there. Exact-line-search BFGS, initialized with the identity matrix and started inside that ball, converges Q-superlinearly, yet no fixed power greater than one controls all sufficiently late adjacent errors.
tldr: This paper addresses a foundational question in classical numerical optimization about the convergence rate of BFGS with exact line search, finding the minimal adjacent-iterate Q-order to be one.
motivation: To settle Powell's question on whether smoothness assumptions in superlinear convergence force a fixed power law between adjacent iterates of variable-metric methods.
method: Constructs infinitely differentiable, globally strongly convex objectives with bounded Hessian deviation from identity, and analyzes exact-line-search BFGS initialized with identity.
result: Demonstrates that in any finite dimension ≥2, a single nonterminating run attains Q-superlinear convergence with no fixed power greater than one controlling late adjacent errors.
conclusion: Answers Powell's question negatively, showing that the classical smoothness assumptions do not enforce a positive power law for BFGS.

title: Behavior Of The Srb Entropy Functional In Families Of Hyperbolic Attractors And Expanding Maps
authors: Miaohua Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the current state of the study of the SRB entropy functional over open components of families of uniformly hyperbolic systems, including Anosov systems, hyperbolic attractors, expanding maps, and Markov transformations. We address problems concerning the functional's infimum, supremum, and local extrema; the gradient flow induced by the functional; and the functional's behavior near the boundary of open components.
tldr: The paper reviews the behavior of the SRB entropy functional across families of uniformly hyperbolic systems, discussing its extrema and gradient flow within the context of classical dynamical systems.
motivation: To consolidate current understanding of the SRB entropy functional's properties, which is important for analyzing the statistical behavior of hyperbolic dynamical systems.
method: A review of existing results, including Anosov systems, hyperbolic attractors, expanding maps, and Markov transformations, focusing on the entropy functional's infimum, supremum, and local extrema, as well as its gradient flow and boundary behavior.
result: Summarizes state-of-the-art knowledge about the functional's variation across parameter families and identifies open problems.
conclusion: The study of the SRB entropy functional remains an active area in dynamical systems, but it is unrelated to the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Entropy On Regular Sets And Periodic-orbit Growth For Singular Flows
authors: C. A. Morales
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study entropy and periodic-orbit growth for flows on metric spaces. First, we prove that the finite topological entropy of a flow on a compact metric space is completely carried by compact subsets of its regular set. Next, we establish a Bowen--Walters inequality for geometrically separating flows on possibly noncompact metric spaces, under uniform control at time zero and dynamical isolation at infinity. As applications, we obtain the Bowen--Walters inequality for singular suspension flows over expansive homeomorphisms, multisingular-hyperbolic sets---extending the upper-bound part of ---and asymptotically sectional-hyperbolic attractors such as Rovella's .
tldr: This paper studies topological entropy and periodic-orbit growth for flows on metric spaces, showing that finite entropy concentrates on regular sets and deriving Bowen-Walters inequalities for certain singular flows.
motivation: The motivation is to understand how topological entropy is distributed in dynamical systems and to extend entropy inequalities to singular flows, which are less understood.
method: The authors prove that finite topological entropy is carried by compact subsets of the regular set, and establish a Bowen-Walters inequality for geometrically separating flows under specific conditions.
result: They obtain Bowen-Walters inequalities for singular suspension flows and for asymptotic sectional-hyperbolic attractors, extending previous upper-bound results.
conclusion: The results provide insight into entropy and orbit growth for singular flows, advancing the theory of dynamical systems.

title: Empirical Variational Principles For Preimage Entropies
authors: Yi Yang Tao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preimage entropy measures the complexity generated by the inverse-image structure of a non-invertible dynamical system. For a continuous map [MATH] on a compact metric space, Hurley's pointwise topological preimage entropies [MATH] and [MATH] are natural invariants measuring the complexity of preimage sets. The question of whether they admit unconditional variational principles in terms of suitable measure-theoretic counterparts remains open. In this paper we resolve it by using empirical metric preimage entropies [MATH] and [MATH], defined by restricting preimage fibers to orbit segments whose empirical measures are close to a prescribed invariant measure [MATH]. We prove the variational principles $[MATH][MATH]h_{m,\mu}(f)[MATH]\mu[MATH]h^*_{p,\mu}(f)\ge h_{m,\mu}(f)[MATH]f[MATH]\mu[MATH][MATH][MATH]h_{m,\mu}(f)[MATH]h_m(f)[MATH]h_{m,\mu}(f)$ holds. Finally, we establish corresponding variational principles for preimage pressure and give an example showing that uniform separation of preimages does not imply forward expansiveness.

method: Introduces empirical metric preimage entropies restricting preimage fibers to orbit segments with empirical measures close to a prescribed invariant measure, and proves variational principles.
result: Proves the variational principles for preimage entropy and preimage pressure, and shows that uniform separation of preimages does not imply forward expansiveness.

title: Extending Subsampling To Sequential Stopping
authors: Jose Blanchet, Peter Glynn, Wenhao Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fixed-width sequential stopping rules terminate a stochastic simulation once an estimated confidence interval reaches a prescribed width. Classical fixed-width theory typically relies on a strongly consistent estimator of the asymptotic variance. This makes the normalized stopping time asymptotically deterministic, allowing fixed-sample-size limit theory to be transferred to the estimator at termination. This mechanism can fail when simulation output has infinite variance or long-range dependence. Although self-normalization and subsampling can yield asymptotically valid confidence intervals at a fixed sample size, the scaling process and the stopping time may retain nondegenerate randomness, so fixed-sample-size quantiles need not provide valid coverage at termination. In this paper, we develop a unified framework based on a joint functional limit theorem for the estimation process and a scaling process. We characterize the asymptotic behavior of both the stopping time and the self-normalized estimator evaluated at termination, thereby obtaining asymptotically valid sequential confidence intervals in classical finite-variance and infinite-variance settings. Moreover, we introduce a sequential subsampling procedure that consistently estimates the distribution relevant at the stopping time without directly estimating nuisance parameters in the limit distribution. The framework is verified for heavy-tailed moving-average processes, stochastic approximation, and an M/G/1 queue with heavy-tailed service times.
tldr: This paper extends subsampling methods to sequential stopping for stochastic simulation, providing asymptotically valid confidence intervals under infinite variance or long-range dependence.
motivation: Classical fixed-width sequential stopping relies on consistent variance estimators, which fail for processes with infinite variance or long-range dependence, motivating a new framework.
method: The authors develop a unified framework based on a joint functional limit theorem for the estimation and scaling processes, and introduce a sequential subsampling procedure to estimate the distribution at the stopping time without nuisance parameters.
result: They characterize the asymptotic behavior of the stopping time and self-normalized estimator, achieving valid sequential confidence intervals in finite and infinite variance settings, verified for heavy-tailed moving-average processes, stochastic approximation, and M/G/1 queues.
conclusion: The framework generalizes sequential stopping theory and offers a robust method for simulation output with heavy tails or dependence, but is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: Low-Thrust Trajectory Optimization With Quantum Computing And Sequential Convex Programming
authors: Carmine Giordano
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-thrust trajectory optimization is a central task in interplanetary mission design, but its nonlinear dynamics and operational constraints often lead to challenging non-convex optimal-control problems. Sequential convex programming has emerged as an effective approach to address these problems, while quantum annealing offers a complementary paradigm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problems. This paper introduces quSCP, a quantum-based sequential convex programming framework that reformulates each convex subproblem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem suitable for quantum and hybrid quantum--classical solvers. Equality, inequality, and trust-region constraints are embedded through quadratic penalty terms, while an iterative refinement strategy is used to reduce the accuracy loss introduced by binary discretization. The method is assessed on a fuel-optimal Earth--Mars low-thrust transfer by comparing standard sequential convex programming, a continuous quadratic unconstrained formulation, direct quantum processing unit sampling, and D-Wave hybrid solvers. Results show that quSCP produces physically consistent trajectories with propellant consumption and nonlinear constraint violations close to classical benchmarks. Direct quantum annealing is feasible only for small instances because of embedding overhead and hardware connectivity limits, whereas hybrid solvers scale to larger discretizations. Although no computational quantum advantage is demonstrated with current hardware, the results show that quantum and hybrid quantum--classical optimization can already provide competitive solutions for demanding trajectory design problems.
tldr: This paper presents quSCP, a framework that combines quantum annealing with sequential convex programming for low-thrust trajectory optimization, achieving competitive results but no quantum advantage.
motivation: Low-thrust trajectory optimization involves non-convex optimal-control problems; quantum annealing offers a potential complementary approach to classical sequential convex programming.
method: The method reformulates convex subproblems as QUBO problems with penalty terms for constraints, uses iterative refinement to mitigate discretization errors, and employs quantum, hybrid, and classical solvers for comparison.
result: quSCP produces physically consistent trajectories with propellant consumption and constraint violations close to classical results; direct quantum annealing is limited to small instances due to hardware constraints, while hybrid solvers scale better.
conclusion: Quantum and hybrid quantum-classical optimization can already provide competitive solutions for demanding trajectory design, though computational quantum advantage is not yet achieved with current hardware.

title: Doffo_tr: A Decentralized Objective Function-Free Optimization Method With Trust-Region
authors: Stefania Bellavia, Greta Malaspina, Benedetta Morini
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel objective function-free trust-region method designed to solve optimization problems over decentralized networks. Unlike traditional approaches that often rely on stepsize tuning, our framework employs a function-free trust-region procedure that enables adaptive selection of the step length. Our approach accommodates first- and second-order models and eliminates the need to share local function values and gradients among agents, thereby enhancing privacy and computational efficiency. On the theoretical side, we establish provable iteration complexity guarantees that, for some variants, match those established for classical centralized trust-region methods. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that our approach achieves a favorable trade-off between performance and efficiency, requiring only moderate communication overhead compared to state-of-the-art methods in the literature.
tldr: The paper presents a decentralized trust-region optimization method that avoids sharing objective function values and gradients, enhancing privacy while achieving competitive convergence guarantees.
motivation: Traditional decentralized optimization methods often require sharing sensitive local data (function values, gradients) across agents, which raises privacy concerns and incurs communication overhead. A method that eliminates the need for such sharing could improve privacy and efficiency.
method: The authors introduce Doffo_tr, a function-free trust-region framework that adaptively selects step lengths without relying on local function values or gradients. It supports both first- and second-order models and operates over decentralized networks.
result: The method provides iteration complexity guarantees, some variants matching classical centralized trust-region methods. Numerical experiments show a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off with moderate communication overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: Doffo_tr offers a privacy-preserving and efficient solution for decentralized optimization, demonstrating that function-free trust-region methods can be both theoretically sound and practically competitive.

title: Partially Observed Mean Field Games Without Perfect Recall: Optimality Conditions And Equilibria
authors: Xuanping Zhang, Xiao Zhang, Wang Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.00880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies partially observed mean field games without perfect recall (WPR). The representative agent observes a noisy signal, but the control at time \(t\) uses only \(\mathcal G_t^I=\sigma(y_t)\), a generally non-nested information family. The conditional population law instead uses the observation filtration \(\mathbb F^Y\). These coupled levels rely on different information scales and are difficult to close within one construction. We parameterize the environment by a deterministic compatible joint law of state, driving variables, and random mean field term, thereby preserving its dependence structure without enlarging the agent's control information. For a fixed law, a reference measure and Girsanov's theorem yield a WPR stochastic maximum principle; the selected response is represented by the conditional Hamiltonian and WPR belief measure. The joint path posterior of hidden state and mean field term gives a weak Kushner-Stratonovich representation of the conditional population law. A recursive response map is continuous on a compact convex set of compatible laws, so Schauder-Tychonoff yields a weak WPR equilibrium. For a fixed equilibrium law and feedback, a compatible Yamada-Watanabe theorem lifts pathwise uniqueness to a strong realization. Finally, a linear-quadratic interbank lending example compares perfect recall (PR) with WPR. The PR response follows the Kalman-Bucy feedback, whereas the WPR response solves a Fredholm-Volterra equation and is affine in the current observation under Gaussianity. The numerical experiment illustrates how equilibrium behavior differs between PR and WPR.
tldr: This paper studies partially observed mean field games without perfect recall, establishing optimality conditions and equilibria via a stochastic maximum principle.
motivation: To model systems where agents have incomplete information and imperfect memory, common in economics and finance.
method: The authors parameterize the environment by a deterministic compatible joint law, use Girsanov's theorem for a stochastic maximum principle, and apply Schauder-Tychonoff to prove existence of equilibria.
result: They obtain weak equilibria and strong solutions via a Yamada-Watanabe theorem; a linear-quadratic example shows differences between perfect recall and without perfect recall.
conclusion: This provides a framework for mean field games with partial observation and imperfect recall, though highly specialized.

title: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design Of A Lightweight Pcg Equalizer With A Fixed Step Size For Massive Mimo
authors: Junshuo Wang, Shuting Liu, Shihan Wang, Yan Tian, Jienan Chen
